chapter1.word: Find the error: "I don't need nobody's advice."
chapter1.explanation: Double negative + wrong possessive placement; correct: "I don't need nobody else's advice" (else takes the 's), though best style avoids double negative altogether.

chapter1.word: Find the error: "He gave me many informations about the exam."
chapter1.explanation: Information is uncountable; use "much information" or "many pieces of information".

chapter1.word: Find the error: "Every boy, girl and teacher are present."
options: Every boy, girl and teacher are
chapter1.explanation: 'Every', even before multiple nouns joined by 'and', takes a singular verb → "is present".

chapter1.word: Find the error: "He bought a hundred rupees note."
chapter1.explanation: Number+unit acting as adjective before a noun stays singular → "a hundred rupee note".

chapter1.word: Find the error: "Priya is my cousin sister."
chapter1.explanation: 'Cousin sister' is redundant in English → "my cousin".

chapter1.word: Find the error: "My two brother-in-laws live in Pune."
chapter1.explanation: In compound nouns, the main/root word takes the plural → "brothers-in-law".

chapter1.word: Find the error: "None of the option was correct."
chapter1.explanation: 'One of/none of' select from a plural group → "None of the options".

chapter1.word: Find the error: "This is the best creative of Da Vinci."
chapter1.explanation: After a superlative adjective, a noun is required, not an adjective → "the best creation".

chapter1.word: Find the error: "The scissor is lying on the table."
chapter1.explanation: Pair-nouns like scissors, trousers, tongs are always plural → "The scissors are".

chapter1.word: Find the error: "David's and Mindy's car is new."
chapter1.explanation: For joint possession of one item, 's is added only to the last name → "David and Mindy's".

chapter1.word: Find the error: "We saw ten deers grazing in the field."
chapter1.explanation: Deer, sheep, fish, aircraft have same singular/plural form → "ten deer".

chapter1.word: Find the error: "The table's legs are broken."
chapter1.explanation: Non-living objects don't take 's; use 'of' → "The legs of the table".

chapter1.word: Find the error: "He is doctor by profession."
chapter1.explanation: Professions require an article → "a doctor".

chapter1.word: Fill in the blank: "His mathematics ______ very weak."
chapter1.explanation: Determiner-shift exception — 'his mathematics' means calculations/data, so it becomes plural → "are".

chapter1.word: Find the error: "He is five months old."
chapter1.explanation: Unit acting as adjective stays singular → "five month old".

chapter1.word: Find the error: "I bought two dozens mangoes."
chapter1.explanation: With a number before it, 'dozen/hundred' stays singular → "two dozen mangoes".

chapter1.word: Find the error: "He has a strong believe in God."
chapter1.explanation: 'Believe' is a verb; the noun form is 'belief' → "a strong belief".

chapter1.word: Find the error: "She gave me a useful advice about my career."
chapter1.explanation: Advice is uncountable — never takes 'a/an'. Correct: "useful advice" or "a useful piece of advice."

chapter1.word: Find the error: "Cities after cities were destroyed."
chapter1.explanation: Noun+preposition+same noun pattern is always singular → "City after city".

chapter1.word: Find the error: "Please explain the plan in details."
chapter1.explanation: Fixed idiom is "in detail", not "in details".

chapter1.word: Fill in the blank: "A thief has stolen my ______." (belonging/belongings)
chapter1.explanation: 'Belongings' is always plural, no singular form used this way.

chapter1.word: Find the error: "The police was investigating the matter."
chapter1.explanation: Police, cattle, people, gentry, peasantry always take plural verb → "were".

chapter1.word: Find the error: "Most of the feedbacks were positive."
chapter1.explanation: 'Feedback' is uncountable → "Most of the feedback".

chapter1.word: Find the error: "Every members of the alumni attended the event."
chapter1.explanation: 'Every' takes a singular noun → "Every member".

chapter1.word: Find the error: "The poor's honesty impressed everyone."
chapter1.explanation: "The + adjective" (a group) never takes 's → "The honesty of the poor".

chapter1.word: Find the error: "Mathematics are a tough subject."
chapter1.explanation: Subject names (Mathematics, Physics, Economics) look plural but take singular verb → "is".

chapter1.word: Find the error: "The outskirts has developed rapidly."
chapter1.explanation: 'Outskirts' is always plural → "The outskirts have".

chapter1.word: Find the error: "There have been heavy rain falls this week."
chapter1.explanation: 'Rainfall' is one uncountable word, no plural → "heavy rainfall".

chapter1.word: Find the error: "This is the boys's hostel."
chapter1.explanation: Plural nouns ending in 's' take only an apostrophe, not 's → "boys'".

chapter1.word: Fill in the blank: He bought all the ______ needed for the lab.
chapter1.explanation: 'Equipment' is uncountable, never takes plural 's'.

chapter2.word: Find the error: "The baby was delivered and the mother looked at him."
options: and the mother looked at him
chapter2.explanation: Gender-unknown infants take 'it' → "looked at it".

chapter2.word: Find the error: "I want your favour."
chapter2.explanation: 'Favour' does not take a possessive before it → "favour from you".

chapter2.word: Find the error: "Here is the toy what I was looking for."
chapter2.explanation: After 'the same/only/all/superlative', 'that' is compulsory → "that I was looking for" (here 'toy' + specific reference also favours 'that').

chapter2.word: Find the error: "Judy solved the difficult problem by her own."
chapter2.explanation: Correct structure is "on her own" or "by herself", not "by her own".

chapter2.word: Find the error: "They told me that neither of them were present."
options: that neither of them were present
chapter2.explanation: 'Neither of' takes a singular verb → "was present".

chapter2.word: Find the error: "The climate of Delhi is far better than Mumbai."
chapter2.explanation: Comparing climate to a city is illogical; use 'that of' → "than that of Mumbai".

chapter2.word: Find the error: "Your's sincerely,"
chapter2.explanation: Possessive pronouns never take an apostrophe → "Yours".

chapter2.word: Find the error: "The children slept themselves peacefully."
chapter2.explanation: 'Sleep' never takes a reflexive pronoun → "The children slept".

chapter2.word: Find the error: "Switzerland lies among Germany, France, Austria and Italy."
chapter2.explanation: For fixed geographical borders even among more than two, 'between' is used → "lies between".

chapter2.word: Find the error: "Raj and myself went to the market."
chapter2.explanation: 'Myself' cannot replace 'I' as subject → "Raj and I".

chapter2.word: Find the error: "My father does not like me going outside."
chapter2.explanation: Before a gerund, possessive adjective is used → "my going".

chapter2.word: Find the error: "All citizens should love each other."
chapter2.explanation: 'Each other' is for two; for more than two, use 'one another'.

chapter2.word: Find the error: "I saw a man whom was wearing a coat."
chapter2.explanation: Subject of the clause needs 'who', not 'whom' → "who was wearing".

chapter2.word: Find the error: "The fish who Gopal caught was huge."
chapter2.explanation: For animals/things, 'which' is used, not 'who' → "The fish which Gopal caught".

chapter2.word: Find the error: "This aspects will be tested in the exam."
chapter2.explanation: 'This' is singular; plural noun 'aspects' needs 'These'.

chapter2.word: Find the error: "...everyone but he was happy to receive the gift."
chapter2.explanation: 'But' functioning as a preposition (meaning except) takes objective case → "everyone but him".

chapter2.word: Find the error: "One must keep his promises."
chapter2.explanation: 'One' must be followed consistently by 'one's' → "one's promises".

chapter2.word: Find the error: "The dog hurt it's leg."
chapter2.explanation: Possessive form is 'its' (no apostrophe); "it's" = it is/has.

chapter2.word: Find the error: "The few people who came to my party are the only friends."
chapter2.explanation: After 'the few', relative pronoun 'that' is preferred → "that came".

chapter2.word: Find the error: "It is me who helped you."
chapter2.explanation: After "It is/was", subjective case is used → "It is I".

chapter2.word: Find the error: "My mother gave us some cake to eat it."
chapter2.explanation: After an infinitive, a redundant object is not used → "to eat".

chapter2.word: Find the error: "Peter did not speak to no one."
chapter2.explanation: Two negatives are not used together → "to anyone".

chapter2.word: Find the error: "Between you and I, this is a secret."
chapter2.explanation: Object of preposition 'between' takes objective case → "you and me".

chapter2.word: Find the error: "His house is smaller than you."
chapter2.explanation: Comparing 'his house' to 'you' is illogical; must compare like with like → "than yours".

chapter2.word: Find the error: "This is the place here Sudhir found the wallet."
chapter2.explanation: For place, the relative adverb 'where' is used → "where Sudhir found".

chapter2.word: Find the error: "He is a man who word is his bond."
chapter2.explanation: Possession requires 'whose', not 'who' → "whose word".

chapter2.word: Find the error: "The minister and his cabinet members absented himself from the meeting."
options: The minister and his cabinet members
chapter2.explanation: Subject is plural (minister + members), so reflexive must be plural → "absented themselves".

chapter2.word: Find the error: "Except for you and I, no one knew the truth."
chapter2.explanation: After a preposition (except), objective case is used → "you and me".

chapter2.word: Find the error: "Everybody has come on time, hasn't he?"
chapter2.explanation: Indefinite pronouns take a singular verb in the sentence but a plural pronoun in the question tag → "haven't they?"

chapter2.word: Find the error: "Each employee must adhere to their code."
chapter2.explanation: 'Each' is singular and takes his/her, not their → "his/her code".

chapter2.word: Find the error: "Me and my friends often go to the park."
chapter2.explanation: Good-sense order rule (231): others first, self last → "My friends and I".

chapter2.word: Find the error: "This is the boy who he stole the purse."
chapter2.explanation: Relative pronoun 'who' is itself the subject; adding 'he' is redundant → "who stole the purse".

chapter2.word: Find the error: "Each of the boys have completed their assignment."
chapter2.explanation: 'Each of' + plural noun still takes singular verb and singular pronoun → "has completed his assignment".

chapter2.word: Fill in the blank: "______ being a rainy day, I did not go to school."
chapter2.explanation: Pseudo/dummy subject 'It' is used for weather/time sentences with no real subject.

chapter2.word: Find the error: "I enjoyed me during the holidays."
chapter2.explanation: 'Enjoy' always takes a reflexive pronoun → "enjoyed myself".

chapter3.word: Arrange correctly: (Indian / wooden / beautiful / old / red) box
options: Indian old red beautiful wooden box
beautiful old red Indian wooden box
red beautiful old Indian wooden box
wooden old red beautiful Indian box
chapter3.explanation: OSASCOMP order: Opinion(beautiful) → Age(old) → Colour(red) → Origin(Indian) → Material(wooden).

chapter3.word: Find the error: "I don't have some experience of this field."
chapter3.explanation: Negative sentences take 'any', not 'some' → "any experience".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "He was a very wiser ruler."
chapter3.explanation: 'Very' goes with positive degree, not comparative → "a very wise ruler".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "He secured the first highest marks."
chapter3.explanation: 'Highest' is already first; "first highest" is redundant → "the highest marks".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "I am stressed by the noise and it is very stressed."
options: I am stressed by the noise
chapter3.explanation: The cause of feeling takes "-ful/-ing" form → "very stressful".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "She is more smarter than her sister."
chapter3.explanation: Double comparative is wrong → "smarter".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "It violated the principle rights."
chapter3.explanation: 'Principal' (main) is the adjective; 'principle' is a noun → "the principal rights".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "He is so weak to lift the box."
chapter3.explanation: 'Too...to' expresses inability, not 'so...to' → "too weak to".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "Sameer gave very less information."
chapter3.explanation: Without a comparison, 'little' is used with uncountables, not 'less' → "very little information".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "Rahul is taller than any boy in class."
chapter3.explanation: To exclude the subject from its own group, 'other' is needed → "than any other boy".

chapter3.word: Fill in the blank: "There is only a ______ quantity of food left."
chapter3.explanation: 'Quantity' always takes 'small', a fixed collocation.

chapter3.word: Find the error: "She is more tall than her brother."
chapter3.explanation: One-syllable adjectives take '-er', not 'more' → "taller".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "I would love to have the later one."
chapter3.explanation: For "the second of two", use 'latter', not 'later' → "the latter one".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "He is an most excellent student."
chapter3.explanation: Absolute adjective 'excellent' cannot take 'most' → "an excellent student".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "Please explain the plan in very details."
chapter3.explanation: Fixed idiom is "in great detail".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "New Delhi is hotter to Chandigarh."
chapter3.explanation: Comparatives take 'than', not 'to' → "than Chandigarh".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "I have a marker in every hand."
chapter3.explanation: 'Each' (not 'every') is used for exactly two → "in each hand".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "She sings as better as Elena."
chapter3.explanation: 'As...as' takes positive degree → "as well as".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "We should respect the elder people."
chapter3.explanation: For elderly people in society (not blood relation), 'elderly' is correct → "the elderly people".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "This is three times larger than that."
chapter3.explanation: 'Times' takes 'as...as', not comparative → "three times as large as that".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "The higher you go, cooler it gets."
chapter3.explanation: Parallel comparatives both need 'the' → "the cooler it gets".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "Among all the students, he is the better."
chapter3.explanation: Comparison among 3+ needs superlative → "the best".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "I can assure you that this school is most excellent."
options: that this school is most excellent
chapter3.explanation: 'Excellent' is a non-gradable/absolute adjective → "is excellent".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "85% of them saw it as essentials."
chapter3.explanation: Adjectives never take plural 's' → "as essential".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "He made a quickly decision without facts."
chapter3.explanation: A noun needs an adjective, not an adverb → "a quick decision".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "Rahul is stronger and wise than Mahesh."
chapter3.explanation: Both adjectives joined by 'and' must be in the same (comparative) degree → "and wiser".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "I had to choose the best of the two options."
options: the best of the two options
chapter3.explanation: Choosing between exactly two takes comparative, not superlative → "the better of the two".

chapter3.word: Fill in the blank: "The survivors were thrown still ______ back into barbarism."
chapter3.explanation: 'Further' is used for abstract/figurative extension, not physical distance.

chapter3.word: Find the error: "We spent an enjoying day."
chapter3.explanation: For a thing causing enjoyment, use "-able" form → "an enjoyable day".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "No less than fifty students were absent."
chapter3.explanation: Countable nouns take 'fewer', not 'less' → "No fewer than fifty students".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "He is faster than smarter."
chapter3.explanation: Comparing two qualities of the same person uses 'more', not '-er' → "more fast than smart".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "David looks older to he really is."
chapter3.explanation: 'Older' (general age) takes 'than', not 'to' → "than he really is".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "He is more stronger than Ajay."
chapter3.explanation: Double comparative is wrong; to intensify use 'much/far' → "much stronger than Ajay".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "He is taller and most handsome."
chapter3.explanation: Adjectives joined by 'and' should be in the same degree → "and more handsome".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "The painting is the most unique piece."
chapter3.explanation: 'Unique' is an absolute adjective; no degree is possible → "the unique piece".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "He has solved the five first questions of the exercise."
chapter3.explanation: Order is Ordinal before Cardinal → "the first five questions".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "He is a quick runner and a smart think."
chapter3.explanation: For a person, noun form is needed → "a smart thinker".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "She was not enough tall to reach it."
chapter3.explanation: 'Enough' follows the adjective → "tall enough".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "Injured were taken to the hospital."
chapter3.explanation: "The + adjective" denotes the whole class → "The injured were taken".

chapter3.word: Find the error: "This deal was more preferable than that."
chapter3.explanation: 'Preferable' is inherently comparative; takes 'to', not 'more...than' → "preferable to that".

chapter4.word: Find the error: "I am having a car."
chapter4.explanation: 'Have' meaning possession is stative → "I have a car".

chapter4.word: Find the error: "She failed meeting the deadline."
chapter4.explanation: 'Fail' takes infinitive → "failed to meet the deadline".

chapter4.word: Find the error: "We heard him to say very mean things."
chapter4.explanation: After verbs of perception (hear, see), bare infinitive is used → "heard him say".

chapter4.word: Find the error: "Walking in the park, a tree fell."
chapter4.explanation: The participle's subject differs from the main clause's subject (dangling modifier) → "While he was walking in the park, a tree fell."

chapter4.word: Find the error: "I used to playing cricket every Sunday."
chapter4.explanation: 'Used to' (past habit) takes base verb → "used to play".

chapter4.word: Find the error: "As she may speak several languages, she got the job."
options: As she may speak several languages
chapter4.explanation: Ability is shown by 'can', not 'may' → "As she can speak".

chapter4.word: Find the error: "Having caught, the thief admitted stealing a purse."
options: the thief admitted stealing a purse
chapter4.explanation: The thief was caught (passive sense), so "Having been caught" is needed.

chapter4.word: Find the error: "All of us are looking forward to join his new company."
options: All of us are looking forward
chapter4.explanation: 'Looking forward to' (fixed phrase) takes gerund → "to joining".

chapter4.word: Find the error: "He didn't went to Rome."
chapter4.explanation: After 'did/didn't', the main verb stays in base form → "didn't go".

chapter4.word: Find the error: "He denied to help me."
chapter4.explanation: 'Deny' takes gerund → "denied helping me".

chapter4.word: Find the error: "He was considering to apply for the post."
chapter4.explanation: 'Consider' takes a gerund, not infinitive → "considering applying".

chapter4.word: Find the error: "If you earn a decent income, you dare help the poor."
options: If you earn a decent income
chapter4.explanation: Moral advice needs 'ought to/should' → "you ought to help the poor".

chapter4.word: Find the error: "I consider him as one of my closest friends."
chapter4.explanation: After 'consider', 'as' is not used → "I consider him one of my closest friends".

chapter4.word: Fill in the blank: "He stopped ______ to answer the phone (while working)."
chapter4.explanation: 'Stopped working' means he paused the work he was doing to answer the phone (V-ing = stopped doing that activity).

chapter4.word: Find the error: "He decided going on a trip to Manali."
options: going on a trip to Manali
chapter4.explanation: 'Decide' takes infinitive, not gerund → "decided to go".

chapter4.word: Find the error: "I am looking forward to meet you."
chapter4.explanation: 'To' here is a preposition (fixed phrase), so gerund follows → "to meeting you".

chapter4.word: Find the error: "I am used to work in night shifts."
chapter4.explanation: 'Be used to' (be accustomed to) takes gerund → "used to working".

chapter4.word: Find the error: "Being a rainy day, we decided not to go out."
options: we decided not to go out
chapter4.explanation: For weather sentences, dummy subject 'It' must be added → "It being a rainy day".

chapter4.word: Find the error: "The company will not rise the taxes."
chapter4.explanation: 'Raise' (transitive - to raise something) is needed, not 'rise' → "raise the taxes".

chapter4.word: Find the error: "This book is worth to read."
chapter4.explanation: 'Worth' is followed by a gerund → "worth reading".

chapter4.word: Find the error: "How dare you to say these words?"
chapter4.explanation: 'Dare' as modal takes base verb, no 'to' → "How dare you say".

chapter4.word: Find the error: "I can to help you."
chapter4.explanation: After a modal, 'to' is not used → "I can help you".

chapter4.word: Find the error: "He shutted the door loudly."
chapter4.explanation: 'Shut' has the same form in V1/V2/V3 → "He shut the door".

chapter4.word: Find the error: "The new bridge will be broadcasted on TV tonight."
chapter4.explanation: 'Broadcast' has same V2/V3 form → "will be broadcast".

chapter4.word: Find the error: "Walking in the park, a snake bit him."
chapter4.explanation: Dangling modifier — the snake wasn't the one walking → "While he was walking in the park, a snake bit him."

chapter4.word: Find the error: "He went there for meeting his friend."
chapter4.explanation: Purpose is shown by 'to + V1', not 'for + V-ing' → "to meet his friend".

chapter4.word: Find the error: "He is going to lay down."
chapter4.explanation: To lie oneself down (intransitive) is 'lie', not 'lay' → "to lie down".

chapter4.word: Find the error: "The sweet tasted deliciously."
chapter4.explanation: After stative sense-verbs (taste, smell, feel), an adjective is used, not adverb → "tasted delicious".

chapter4.word: Find the error: "She is owning a scooty."
chapter4.explanation: 'Own' is a stative verb; no continuous form → "She owns".

chapter4.word: Find the error: "She made me to laugh."
chapter4.explanation: Causative 'make' (active) takes bare infinitive → "made me laugh".

chapter5.word: Find the error: "Scientists believed that gravity pulled down everything."
chapter5.explanation: Universal truths stay in simple present, regardless of the reporting verb's tense → "gravity pulls".

chapter5.word: Find the error: "By next year, she will be completed her research."
options: she will be completed her research
chapter5.explanation: Future deadline needs future perfect → "will have completed".

chapter5.word: Find the error: "You always disturb me, it's so annoying."
chapter5.explanation: For annoying habits, continuous tense is used instead of simple present → "You are always disturbing me".

chapter5.word: Find the error: "If he had studied, he would pass the exam."
chapter5.explanation: Type 3 (unfulfilled past) needs 'would have + V3' → "would have passed".

chapter5.word: Find the error: "The company has launched its new product two months ago."
options: its new product two months ago
chapter5.explanation: A definite past time marker ('ago') requires simple past, not present perfect → "launched".

chapter5.word: Find the error: "The train left before we reached the station."
chapter5.explanation: The earlier of two past actions takes past perfect → "had left".

chapter5.word: Find the error: "If you will call me, I will give you the address."
options: I will give you the address
chapter5.explanation: 'If' clause never takes 'will' → "If you call me".

chapter5.word: Find the error: "Hardly had she thrown the ball than it fell."
options: Hardly had she thrown the ball
chapter5.explanation: 'Hardly...when', not 'than' → "when it fell".

chapter5.word: Find the error: "But for your help, I would fail."
chapter5.explanation: 'But for' is a Type 3 condition → "I would have failed".

chapter5.word: Find the error: "If I had money, I would have bought a car."
options: I would have bought a car
chapter5.explanation: A present hypothetical (If + simple past) takes 'would + V1' → "I would buy a car".

chapter5.word: Find the error: "He did not complete his homework yet."
chapter5.explanation: 'Yet' takes present perfect negative → "has not completed".

chapter5.word: Find the error: "It is time you must go home."
chapter5.explanation: After 'it is (high) time', simple past is used → "you went home".

chapter5.word: Find the error: "She has been knowing me since 2005."
chapter5.explanation: 'Know' is a stative verb — no continuous form even with since/for → "has known".

chapter5.word: Find the error: "Shakespeare has written many plays."
chapter5.explanation: Actions of people no longer alive are always in simple past → "Shakespeare wrote".

chapter5.word: Find the error: "I wish I was a bird."
chapter5.explanation: Hypothetical wishes always take 'were' → "I wish I were a bird".

chapter5.word: Find the error: "No sooner had she finished that she received a call."
chapter5.explanation: 'No sooner...than', not 'that' → "than she received a call".

chapter5.word: Find the error: "Everything we looked at so far was useful."
options: Everything we looked at so far
chapter5.explanation: 'So far' requires present perfect → "has been useful".

chapter5.word: Find the error: "She insisted that I took the medicine."
chapter5.explanation: Subjunctive mood after 'insist/demand/suggest that' uses base form → "that I take the medicine".

chapter5.word: Find the error: "Unless you will study, you will fail."
chapter5.explanation: 'Unless' (=if not) never takes 'will' → "Unless you study".

chapter5.word: Find the error: "I am trying to reach him for one hour."
options: I am trying to reach him
chapter5.explanation: An action started in past and continuing needs present perfect continuous → "I have been trying".

chapter6.word: Find the error: "Nothing but the marvellous buildings have the charm."
chapter6.explanation: Real subject is 'Nothing', which is singular → "has the charm".

chapter6.word: Find the error: "One of the boys are missing."
chapter6.explanation: Real subject is 'One' (singular) → "is missing".

chapter6.word: Find the error: "Each participant have performed well."
chapter6.explanation: 'Each' always takes singular verb → "has performed well".

chapter6.word: Find the error: "Aman and Karan has done well."
chapter6.explanation: Two different subjects joined by 'and' take a plural verb → "have done well".

chapter6.word: Find the error: "There is two cats in the room."
chapter6.explanation: With dummy subject 'there', the verb agrees with the real noun that follows → "There are two cats".

chapter6.word: Find the error: "Many a man have tried."
chapter6.explanation: 'Many a' + singular noun takes singular verb → "has tried".

chapter6.word: Find the error: "More than one boys were absent."
chapter6.explanation: 'More than one' takes a singular noun and verb → "More than one boy was absent".

chapter6.word: Find the error: "The number of students are fifty."
chapter6.explanation: 'The number of' takes singular verb (unlike 'a number of') → "is fifty".

chapter6.word: Find the error: "A number of students is waiting outside."
options: A number of students is waiting
chapter6.explanation: 'A number of' (meaning many) takes a plural verb, unlike 'the number of' → "are waiting".

chapter6.word: Find the error: "Bread and butter are a healthy breakfast."
chapter6.explanation: 'Bread and butter' is a single idea → "is a healthy breakfast".

chapter6.word: Find the error: "Mumps cause weak bones in children."
chapter6.explanation: Diseases like mumps/measles/rickets take singular verb → "Mumps causes".

chapter6.word: Find the error: "Five thousand rupees was spent on food and clothes separately."
chapter6.explanation: When an amount is divided/spent separately, the verb becomes plural → "were spent".

chapter6.word: Find the error: "Both the manager and the assistant is present."
options: Both the manager and the assistant
chapter6.explanation: 'Both...and' always takes a plural verb → "are present".

chapter6.word: Find the error: "A sharp fall in the price of jute have led to losses."
options: A sharp fall in the price of jute
chapter6.explanation: The real subject is 'A sharp fall' (singular), not 'jute' → "has led".

chapter6.word: Find the error: "His advice were perfect."
chapter6.explanation: 'Advice' is uncountable, always singular → "His advice was perfect".

chapter6.word: Find the error: "Neither the manager nor the employees has noticed."
options: Neither the manager nor the employees
chapter6.explanation: With 'neither...nor', verb agrees with the nearer subject 'employees' → "have noticed".

chapter6.word: Find the error: "The principal, along with the vice principals, have approved."
options: The principal, along with the vice principals,
chapter6.explanation: 'Along with' doesn't change the number of the subject; verb follows the first subject 'the principal' → "has approved".

chapter6.word: Find the error: "Writing poems have been my hobby."
chapter6.explanation: A gerund phrase as subject always takes a singular verb → "has been".

chapter6.word: Find the error: "Around 30 percent of the Indian population are estimated to be literate."
options: Around 30 percent of the Indian population
chapter6.explanation: Verb agrees with 'population' (singular) → "is estimated".

chapter6.word: Find the error: "What he said are true."
chapter6.explanation: A whole clause acting as subject is treated as singular → "is true".

chapter6.word: Find the error: "The rich is getting richer."
chapter6.explanation: "The + adjective" (a class of people) takes plural verb → "The rich are getting richer".

chapter6.word: Find the error: "My new spectacle is broken."
chapter6.explanation: 'Spectacles' is a pair-noun, always plural → "My new spectacles are broken".

chapter6.word: Find the error: "The police is investigating the matter."
chapter6.explanation: 'Police' is always plural → "The police are investigating".

chapter6.word: Find the error: "Every boy, girl and teacher are present."
chapter6.explanation: 'Every', even before multiple nouns, takes singular verb → "is present".

chapter6.word: Find the error: "The jury is divided in their opinions."
chapter6.explanation: When members of a collective noun disagree (divided), the verb is plural → "The jury are divided".

chapter7.word: Find the error: "She danced graceful on stage."
chapter7.explanation: 'Danced' (verb) needs an adverb → "danced gracefully".

chapter7.word: Fill in the blank: He is ______ strong for a boy his age.
chapter7.explanation: Before an adjective ('strong'), use 'much too', not 'too much' (which goes before nouns).

chapter7.word: Find the error: "She was not enough tall to reach it."
chapter7.explanation: 'Enough' comes after the adjective, not before → "not tall enough".

chapter7.word: Find the error: "He is waking up lately these days."
chapter7.explanation: 'Lately' means 'recently'; 'delayed' is 'late' → "waking up late".

chapter7.word: Find the error: "Tell me where is the city park."
chapter7.explanation: Embedded question order is Subject+Verb → "where the city park is".

chapter7.word: Fill in the blank: Mohan is ______ shy around strangers.
chapter7.explanation: 'Rather' is used for negative/unpleasant qualities like shyness; 'fairly' suits positive qualities.

chapter7.word: Find the error: "That's the restaurant at where we met."
chapter7.explanation: 'Where' already indicates place; don't add 'at' before it → "the restaurant where we met".

chapter7.word: Find the error: "The book was interesting and an easily read."
chapter7.explanation: 'Read' here is a noun, so it needs an adjective, not an adverb → "an easy read".

chapter7.word: Find the error: "He does not have experience enough."
chapter7.explanation: Before a noun, 'enough' comes first → "enough experience".

chapter7.word: Find the error: "The car is moving very fastly."
chapter7.explanation: 'Fastly' does not exist; 'fast' is both adjective and adverb → "very fast".

chapter7.word: Find the error: "Charandas truth confessed."
chapter7.explanation: A verb must be modified by an adverb, not an adjective → "Charandas truthfully confessed."

chapter7.word: Find the error: "I found it much surprising."
chapter7.explanation: 'Very' goes with -ing forms/positive degree; 'much' goes with V3/comparative → "very surprising".

chapter7.word: Fill in the blank: Please don't shout, speak ______, the baby is sleeping.
chapter7.explanation: 'Speak' (verb) needs the adverb 'quietly'; 'quite' means 'to a great extent' and 'quiet' is an adjective.

chapter7.word: Find the error: "He worked very hardly to pass the exam."
chapter7.explanation: 'Hardly' means 'scarcely'; 'with effort' is 'hard' → "worked very hard".

chapter7.word: Find the error: "There is too much sugar in this tea, it's much too sweet."
chapter7.explanation: This sentence is correct: 'too much' + noun (sugar), 'much too' + adjective (sweet).

chapter7.word: Find the error: "The problem would be soon overcome by the team."
chapter7.explanation: Adverbs of time/frequency sit between the helping verb and main verb → "would soon be overcome".

chapter7.word: Find the error: "No sooner the meeting started that everyone objected."
options: No sooner the meeting started that
chapter7.explanation: 'No sooner' requires inversion (had+subject+V3) and pairs with 'than' → "No sooner had the meeting started than".

chapter7.word: Find the error: "The new shop hardly had opened when trouble began."
options: The new shop hardly had opened
chapter7.explanation: 'Hardly' at the start requires inversion → "Hardly had the new shop opened".

chapter7.word: Find the error: "Paresh eats hardly only food."
chapter7.explanation: The fixed idiom is 'hardly any', not 'hardly only' → "hardly any food".

chapter7.word: Find the error: "She is elected as the President of the club."
chapter7.explanation: 'Elect' and 'appoint' don't take 'as' → "She is elected the President."

chapter7.word: Find the error: "Rarely he went there."
chapter7.explanation: Negative adverb 'Rarely' at the start needs inversion → "Rarely did he go there."

chapter7.word: Find the error: "Not a word didn't they speak."
options: Not a word didn't they speak
chapter7.explanation: A negative adverb at the start already inverts the sentence; adding 'didn't' is a double negative → "Not a word did they speak."

chapter7.word: Find the error: "No matter how hard work you."
chapter7.explanation: No inversion in embedded clauses → "how hard you work".

chapter7.word: Find the error: "She was quite embarrassed to speak in public."
chapter7.explanation: When a quality is so extreme that an action becomes impossible, use 'too...to' → "too embarrassed to speak".

chapter7.word: Find the error: "They secret decided to leave."
chapter7.explanation: The verb 'decided' needs the adverb 'secretly' → "secretly decided".

chapter7.word: Find the error: "He is going to abroad next month."
chapter7.explanation: 'Abroad' is itself an adverb of place; no preposition 'to' is needed → "going abroad".

chapter7.word: Find the error: "He has done quite all the work."
chapter7.explanation: 'Quite' and 'all' are never used together → "He has done all the work."

chapter7.word: Find the error: "I am rarely late, isn't it?" (ADV related to negative adverbs)
chapter7.explanation: 'Rarely' already makes the statement negative, so the tag should be positive and refer to 'I' → "am I?"

chapter7.word: Fill in the blank: I was ______ surprised at the sudden news.
chapter7.explanation: 'Much' pairs with past-participle (V3) forms like 'surprised'.

chapter7.word: Fill in the blank: She speaks English very ______.
chapter7.explanation: 'Good' is an adjective; the action of speaking needs the adverb 'well'.

chapter7.word: Find the error: "He speaks English as fluent as a native speaker."
chapter7.explanation: Comparing the verb 'speaks' (an action) needs an adverb → "as fluently as".

chapter7.word: Find the error: "Do you know where does she reside?"
chapter7.explanation: Embedded questions don't invert → "where she resides".

chapter7.word: Find the error: "Suman performed at the festival well yesterday."
chapter7.explanation: Adverb order should be Manner → Place → Time → "performed well at the festival yesterday".

chapter7.word: Find the error: "He always is arriving late."
chapter7.explanation: Frequency adverbs go after 'is/am/are' → "is always arriving".

chapter7.word: Find the error: "Rama can bowl fastly."
chapter7.explanation: No such word as 'fastly' → "Rama can bowl fast."

chapter8.word: Find the error: "This committee comprises of five members."
chapter8.explanation: 'Comprise' (active) never takes 'of' → "comprises five members".

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: The building rests ______ the four huge pillars.
chapter8.explanation: 'Rest on/upon' is fixed with 'depend, rely, count, bank'.

chapter8.word: Find the error: "Enter into the room quietly."
chapter8.explanation: 'Enter' does not take 'into' for physically entering a place → "Enter the room".

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: Excessive smoking is injurious ______ health.
chapter8.explanation: 'Injurious', 'harmful', 'senior', 'junior', 'similar' all take 'to'.

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: I am tired ______ your constant excuses. (Fixed Prep — tired OF)
chapter8.explanation: 'Tired of' is fixed usage.

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: This scholarship scheme is meant ______ economically weak students. (Fixed Prep — meant for)
chapter8.explanation: 'Meant for' is the fixed phrase for purpose/beneficiary.

chapter8.word: Find the error: "I want to thank to Reeta for her help."
chapter8.explanation: 'Thank' never takes 'to' before the person → "thank Reeta".

chapter8.word: Find the error: "I asked the doctor to explain me the cause of my illness."
chapter8.explanation: 'Explain' needs 'to' before a human object → "explain to me the cause".

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: The soldiers marched ______ night.
chapter8.explanation: 'Night' (a farewell/neutral time) takes 'at'.

chapter8.word: Find the error: "Despite of the rain, we went out."
chapter8.explanation: 'Despite' never takes 'of' → "Despite the rain".

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: She had to part ______ her best friend when she moved.
chapter8.explanation: 'Part from' is used for a person, so option should actually be 'from' — Correction: 'part from' a person.

chapter8.word: Find the error: "I supplied him to food and medicines."
options: supplied him to food and medicines
chapter8.explanation: Correct structure is 'supply somebody WITH something' → "supplied him with food and medicines".

chapter8.word: Find the error: "This deal was more preferable than that one."
chapter8.explanation: 'Preferable' is inherently comparative; it takes only 'to', never 'more' or 'than' → "preferable to that one".

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: The prize was divided ______ the three winners.
chapter8.explanation: 'Among' is used for more than two.

chapter8.word: Find the error: "Inspite of buying a new car, I still use my old one."
options: Inspite of buying a new car
I still use my old one
chapter8.explanation: 'Instead of' shows substitution/alternative; 'in spite of' shows contrast — meaning here needs "Instead of buying a new car".

chapter8.word: Find the error: "He was killed with a terrorist."
chapter8.explanation: A living doer in passive voice takes 'by' → "killed by a terrorist".

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: His behaviour is ______ control now.
chapter8.explanation: 'Beyond control/doubt/repair' is fixed.

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: He died ______ cancer last year.
chapter8.explanation: 'Die of' is used for diseases.

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: He walked ______ the tunnel to reach the other side.
chapter8.explanation: 'Through' is used for passing inside something like a tunnel.

chapter8.word: Find the error: "He is married with a doctor."
chapter8.explanation: Active voice 'married' never takes a preposition → "He is married to a doctor" (passive 'to' only).

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: He is blind ______ one eye due to an accident.
chapter8.explanation: 'Blind in' one eye refers to physical blindness.

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: Paper is made ______ wood pulp.
chapter8.explanation: 'Made from' is used when the material undergoes a chemical/complete change.

chapter8.word: Find the error: "Despite of facing a lot of criticism, he continued his work."
options: Despite of facing a lot of criticism
chapter8.explanation: 'Despite' never takes 'of' → "Despite facing a lot of criticism".

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: Please compare your answer ______ mine; they're very similar.
chapter8.explanation: 'Compare with' is used for similar things.

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: The letter was written ______ a pen.
chapter8.explanation: 'With' is used for a lifeless tool/instrument.

chapter8.word: Find the error: "We discussed about the project yesterday."
chapter8.explanation: 'Discuss' never takes 'about' → "discussed the project".

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: My success ______ this project depends ______ your support.
chapter8.explanation: 'Depend on/upon' is fixed; 'success in' a project is standard usage.

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: They have been friends ______ five years.
chapter8.explanation: 'For' is used with a duration/period of time.

chapter8.word: Find the error: "She is capable to handle this project."
chapter8.explanation: 'Capable' takes 'of' + gerund → "capable of handling".

chapter8.word: Find the error: "He proposed his parents that they should travel abroad."
chapter8.explanation: 'Propose' takes 'to' before a human indirect object → "proposed to his parents".

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: I have known her ______ 2010.
chapter8.explanation: 'Since' is used with a fixed point of time (2010); 'for' is used with duration.

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: I go for a walk ______ the morning.
chapter8.explanation: 'Morning' and 'evening' (welcoming times) take 'in'.

chapter8.word: Find the error: "She was born on 1998."
chapter8.explanation: Years take 'in' → "born in 1998".

chapter8.word: Find the error: "The meeting is scheduled at Monday."
chapter8.explanation: Days take 'on' → "scheduled on Monday".

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: We must abstain ______ alcohol during treatment.
chapter8.explanation: 'Abstain', 'refrain', 'prevent', 'differ' (in origin sense) take 'from'.

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: The manager will deal ______ this issue personally.
chapter8.explanation: 'Deal with' is used for handling a situation/person.

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: The soldier died ______ his wounds.
chapter8.explanation: 'Die from' is used for a cause like wounds/overeating/accident.

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: The suspect burst ______ tears during questioning.
chapter8.explanation: 'Burst into tears/laughter' is a fixed phrase.

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: The hall was crowded ______ people.
chapter8.explanation: 'Crowded', 'satisfied', 'pleased', 'familiar' take 'with'.

chapter8.word: Find the error: "His house is farther from mine on this issue."
options: farther from mine on this issue
chapter8.explanation: For abstract/figurative distance, 'further' is used, not 'farther' (physical distance) → "further on this issue" doesn't fit physically either; correct usage: "His argument goes further on this issue."

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: This shop deals ______ electronic goods.
chapter8.explanation: 'Deal in' is used for trading goods.

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: The poet compared life ______ a journey.
chapter8.explanation: 'Compare to' is used for dissimilar/metaphorical things.

chapter8.word: Find the error: "He is superior than his rival in every aspect."
chapter8.explanation: Words ending in '-ior' (superior, senior, junior, prior) take 'to', never 'than' → "superior to his rival".

chapter8.word: Find the error: "I am not aware about the new rules."
options: not aware about the new rules
chapter8.explanation: 'Aware' takes 'of', not 'about' → "aware of the new rules".

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: She was angry ______ the delay in the flight.
chapter8.explanation: 'Angry at' is used for a situation/thing.

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: This chair is made ______ wood.
chapter8.explanation: 'Made of' is used when the original material is still visible (physical change).

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: He complained ______ the noisy neighbours to the police.
chapter8.explanation: 'Complain against' is used for a person; 'complain about' is used for a thing.

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: ______ being talented, he is also very hardworking.
chapter8.explanation: 'Besides' means 'in addition to'.

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: I don't agree ______ you on this matter.
chapter8.explanation: 'Agree with' is used for a person.

chapter8.word: Find the error: "Ram is sitting besides Sita."
chapter8.explanation: 'Beside' means next to; 'besides' means in addition to → "sitting beside Sita".

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: He is devoid ______ common sense.
chapter8.explanation: 'Devoid', 'bereft', 'ashamed', 'aware' all take 'of'.

chapter8.word: Find the error: "Your curry tastes different than the one we had yesterday."
chapter8.explanation: 'Different' takes 'from', not 'than' → "different from the one".

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: He is currently ______ investigation for fraud.
chapter8.explanation: 'Under investigation/pressure/consideration' is fixed.

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: We will meet you ______ tomorrow.
chapter8.explanation: 'Tomorrow', 'today', 'yesterday' take no preposition.

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: He was angry ______ his brother for lying.
chapter8.explanation: 'Angry with' is used for a person.

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: He is completely blind ______ his own faults.
chapter8.explanation: 'Blind to' faults means mentally ignoring them.

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: He was surprised ______ her sudden visit.
chapter8.explanation: 'Surprised', 'shocked', 'laugh', 'good/bad (at a skill)' take 'at'.

chapter8.word: Find the error: "The garden was full with roses."
chapter8.explanation: 'Full' takes 'of', not 'with' → "full of roses".

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: The two countries agreed to ______ into a treaty.
chapter8.explanation: For joining an agreement/debate, 'enter into' is correct (exception to the 'Enter' rule).

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: The old man is hard ______ hearing.
chapter8.explanation: 'Hard of hearing' is a fixed idiom (using 'of').

chapter8.word: Find the error: "He is very fond to eat spicy food."
chapter8.explanation: 'Fond' takes 'of' + gerund → "fond of eating spicy food".

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: This gift is ______ you and me only.
chapter8.explanation: 'Between' is used for exactly two people, paired with 'and'.

chapter8.word: Find the error: "The match was stopped because the heavy rain."
chapter8.explanation: 'Because' (conjunction) takes a clause; before a noun phrase use 'because of' → "because of the heavy rain".

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: She is engrossed ______ her studies these days.
chapter8.explanation: 'Engrossed', 'absorbed', 'involved', 'interested' take 'in'.

chapter8.word: Find the error: "My parents forbade to me from going out at night."
chapter8.explanation: 'Forbade' never takes 'to' before the person → "forbade me from going out".

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: He is known ______ me for many years. (Voice/Preposition fixed list — known TO)
chapter8.explanation: 'Known to' (not 'by') is the fixed passive-voice preposition.

chapter8.word: Find the error: "This job requires someone to rely."
chapter8.explanation: 'Rely' needs 'on' as its object preposition → "someone to rely on".

chapter8.word: Find the error: "The show starts from 9 pm."
chapter8.explanation: 'Start' does not take 'from' → "The show starts at 9 pm."

chapter8.word: Find the error: "He is still coping up with his mother's death."
options: coping up with his mother's death
chapter8.explanation: The correct phrase is 'cope with', not 'cope up with' → "coping with his mother's death".

chapter8.word: Find the error: "The Prime Minister will preside over on the meeting."
chapter8.explanation: 'Preside' takes only 'over', not 'over on' → "preside over the meeting".

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: We must not lean ______ the wet wall.
chapter8.explanation: 'Lean against' is the fixed usage.

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: He finally agreed ______ my proposal.
chapter8.explanation: 'Agree to' is used for a proposal/plan.

chapter8.word: Find the error: "You should dispose off all the extra items."
options: dispose off all the extra items
chapter8.explanation: The correct spelling/preposition is 'dispose of', not 'dispose off' → "dispose of all the extra items".

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: She is eligible ______ this scholarship.
chapter8.explanation: 'Eligible', 'responsible', 'apologise' take 'for'.

chapter8.word: Find the error: "He had no one to talk."
options: He had no one to talk
chapter8.explanation: The infinitive 'to talk' needs its own preposition when it can't take a direct object → "no one to talk to".

chapter8.word: Fill in the blank: It was hard to part ______ my old car.
chapter8.explanation: 'Part with' is used for a thing.

chapter8.word: Find the error: "The police are investigating into the murder case."
chapter8.explanation: 'Investigate' never takes 'into' → "investigating the murder case".

chapter8.word: Find the error: "She was accused for theft in the office."
chapter8.explanation: 'Accused' takes 'of', not 'for' → "accused of theft".

chapter8.word: Find the error: "Please revert back to me by tomorrow."
chapter8.explanation: 'Re-' already means back; 'revert back' is redundant → "revert to me".

chapter8.word: Find the error: "The ball rolled in the yard from the porch."
chapter8.explanation: Motion into a place needs 'into', not the static 'in' → "rolled into the yard".

chapter9.word: Find the error: "Office hours are from 9 AM and 5 PM."
chapter9.explanation: 'From' pairs with 'to', not 'and' → "from 9 AM to 5 PM".

chapter9.word: Find the error: "As I have lived in Mumbai for a year so, I know how expensive it is."
options: As I have lived in Mumbai for a year so
I know how expensive it is
chapter9.explanation: 'As' already introduces the reason clause; adding 'so' is redundant → remove 'so'.

chapter9.word: Fill in the blank: I doubt ______ he will finish the work on time. (Doubt structure — Affirmative uses if/whether)
chapter9.explanation: A plain affirmative expression of doubt takes 'if' or 'whether'.

chapter9.word: Find the error: "I will wait until he will come."
chapter9.explanation: The clause after 'until' never takes 'will' → "until he comes".

chapter9.word: Find the error: "I don't know whether to stay that leave."
chapter9.explanation: 'Whether' pairs with 'or', not 'that' → "whether to stay or leave".

chapter9.word: Find the error: "The reason she is upset is because she broke up with her boyfriend."
chapter9.explanation: With 'The reason...is', use 'that', not 'because' (redundant) → "is that she broke up".

chapter9.word: Fill in the blank: I don't know ______ he will come today or tomorrow.
chapter9.explanation: A choice between two options needs 'whether...or', not 'if'.

chapter9.word: Find the error: "Both Ram and Shyam are not going to the party."
options: Both Ram and Shyam are not going
chapter9.explanation: 'Both' and 'not' cannot be used together; use 'Neither...nor' → "Neither Ram nor Shyam is going".

chapter9.word: Find the error: "Scarcely had the satellite deployed than it transmitted data."
chapter9.explanation: 'Scarcely/Hardly' pair with 'when', not 'than' → "when it transmitted data".

chapter9.word: Find the error: "Since the people decided to leave early, so I had to take a bus."
options: so I had to take a bus
Since the people decided to leave early
chapter9.explanation: Using 'so' after 'Since' at the start is redundant → remove 'so'.

chapter9.word: Find the error: "He recommended replacing the part rather as repairing it."
chapter9.explanation: 'Rather' pairs with 'than', not 'as' → "rather than repairing it".

chapter9.word: Find the error: "Catherine said she loved Heathcliff, however, she could not marry him."
options: however, she could not marry him
chapter9.explanation: Within one sentence, 'but' connects two contrasting clauses; 'however' joins separate sentences → "but she could not marry him".

chapter9.word: Find the error: "Run fast, lest you may not miss the train."
options: lest you may not miss the train
chapter9.explanation: 'Lest' already means 'so that...not'; adding 'not' is a double negative → "lest you should miss the train".

chapter9.word: Fill in the blank: There is no doubt ______ he is talented. (Doubt structure — Negative/Interrogative uses 'that')
chapter9.explanation: 'No doubt' expresses certainty, so it takes 'that'.

chapter9.word: Find the error: "It was so a hot day that we went swimming."
chapter9.explanation: With a countable noun, use 'such a...that', not 'so a' → "such a hot day that".

chapter9.word: Find the error: "I like teaching only such students who are serious."
chapter9.explanation: 'Such' pairs with the relative 'as', not 'who' → "such students as are serious".

chapter9.word: Find the error: "Mrs. Gomathi was that tired and weak that she could scarcely walk."
chapter9.explanation: With adjectives, use 'so...that', not 'that...that' → "so tired and weak that".

chapter9.word: Find the error: "Though he worked hard but he failed."
chapter9.explanation: 'Though' pairs with 'yet' or a comma, never 'but' → "worked hard yet he failed".

chapter9.word: Find the error: "Inspite mother's milk is vital for infants, some avoid it."
chapter9.explanation: A full clause needs 'Although/Though'; 'Despite/In spite of' need only a noun phrase → "Though mother's milk is vital".

chapter9.word: Find the error: "The dumbbells were too heavy that he sprained his wrist."
options: too heavy that he sprained his wrist
chapter9.explanation: 'Too' pairs with 'to', not 'that'; for result use 'so...that' → "so heavy that he sprained his wrist".

chapter9.word: Find the error: "Virat Kohli, not only is a good captain, but is also a great batsman."
options: not only is a good captain, but is also
chapter9.explanation: 'Not only...but also' must join parallel parts placed after the shared verb → "Virat Kohli is not only a good captain but also a great batsman."

chapter9.word: Find the error: "I asked her that where she was going."
chapter9.explanation: 'That' is redundant before a wh-word that already links the clause → "asked her where she was going".

chapter9.word: Find the error: "His marks were so low to get admission."
chapter9.explanation: For an impossible/negative outcome, use 'too...to' → "too low to get admission".

chapter9.word: Find the error: "You cannot expect success until you do not work hard."
options: until you do not work hard
chapter9.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if not'; using 'until...not' is double negative — the intended structure is "unless you work hard".

chapter9.word: Find the error: "It is nothing else than sheer pride."
chapter9.explanation: 'Else' pairs with 'but', not 'than' → "nothing else but sheer pride".

chapter9.word: Find the error: "He is both a writer as well as a teacher."
options: both a writer as well as a teacher
chapter9.explanation: 'Both' pairs only with 'and' → "both a writer and a teacher".

chapter9.word: Find the error: "The game was postponed because heavy rain."
chapter9.explanation: 'Because' (conjunction) needs a full clause; before a noun use 'because of' → "because of heavy rain".

chapter9.word: Find the error: "Helena loves to dig and played in the dirt."
chapter9.explanation: Verbs joined by 'and' must be in the same form → "to dig and play".

chapter9.word: Find the error: "The class is between 8 am to 9 am."
chapter9.explanation: 'Between' pairs with 'and', not 'to' → "between 8 am and 9 am".

chapter9.word: Find the error: "No sooner had the proposal been circulated that objections were raised."
options: No sooner had the proposal been circulated
chapter9.explanation: 'No sooner' pairs with 'than' → "than objections were raised".

chapter10.word: Find the error: "It was one of the biggest landslide in the region's history."
chapter10.explanation: 'One of the' + superlative always takes a plural noun → "biggest landslides".

chapter10.word: Find the error: "nothing like good cup of coffee on a rainy day."
options: nothing like good cup of coffee
chapter10.explanation: Article must go before the adjective 'good' → "a good cup of coffee".

chapter10.word: Fill in the blank: She aspires to become ______ engineer after graduation.
chapter10.explanation: A general profession takes 'a/an'; 'engineer' begins with a vowel sound.

chapter10.word: Find the error: "Please report at the gate no. 6 for your interview."
chapter10.explanation: Numbered items take no article → "at gate no. 6".

chapter10.word: Find the error: "I am going to buy a red car with a leather seats."
options: I am going to buy a red car
chapter10.explanation: 'Seats' is plural, so no 'a/an' is used → "with leather seats".

chapter10.word: Fill in the blank: Tourists visited ______ temple to admire its ancient architecture.
chapter10.explanation: Visiting for a secondary purpose (sightseeing, not worship) requires 'the'.

chapter10.word: Find the error: "I am the most beautiful and a wisest man in the village."
chapter10.explanation: Superlatives always take 'the', not 'a' → "the wisest man".

chapter10.word: Fill in the blank: He wants to climb ______ Mount Everest someday.
chapter10.explanation: Individual mountain peaks take no article.

chapter10.word: Fill in the blank: He is ______ MLA from this constituency.
chapter10.explanation: 'MLA' is pronounced 'em-el-ay', starting with a vowel sound, so 'an' is used.

chapter10.word: Find the error: "Roger was first man to reach the summit."
chapter10.explanation: Ordinals like 'first' always take 'the' → "the first man".

chapter10.word: Find the error: "He went on a journey after the breakfast."
chapter10.explanation: Meals like breakfast, lunch, dinner take no article → "after breakfast".

chapter10.word: Fill in the blank: My grandmother suffers from ______ measles right now.
chapter10.explanation: A few diseases like measles/mumps are exceptions and take 'the'.

chapter10.word: Find the error: "the man is mortal, so he must prepare for death."
options: so he must prepare for death
chapter10.explanation: Universal concepts like 'Man', 'life', 'death' take no article → "Man is mortal".

chapter10.word: Fill in the blank: I waited for ______ hour before he called me back.
chapter10.explanation: 'Many a + singular noun' construction — 'an hour' fits with 'many' omitted for this test; correct fixed phrase is 'many an hour'.

chapter10.word: Find the error: "Who invented telescope in the 17th century?"
chapter10.explanation: Inventions always take 'the' → "invented the telescope".

chapter10.word: Fill in the blank: Abdul Kalam is ______ Newton of India.
chapter10.explanation: When comparing a person to a famous figure metaphorically, 'the' is used.

chapter10.word: Fill in the blank: ______ Ganga is considered sacred in India.
chapter10.explanation: Names of rivers always take 'the'.

chapter10.word: Fill in the blank: She bought ______ European car last year.
chapter10.explanation: 'European' starts with a consonant sound ('y'), so 'a' is used despite the vowel letter.

chapter10.word: Find the error: "He travels to office by the bus every day."
chapter10.explanation: 'By + transport' takes no article → "by bus".

chapter10.word: Find the error: "This is same book like our teacher recommended."
options: same book like our teacher recommended
chapter10.explanation: 'Same' pairs with 'as', and takes 'the' → "the same book as our teacher recommended".

chapter10.word: Fill in the blank: The thief escaped ______ foot before the police arrived. (Fixed phrase — no article)
chapter10.explanation: 'On foot' is a fixed phrase taking no article.

chapter10.word: Fill in the blank: She waited for ______ hour before the doctor arrived.
chapter10.explanation: 'Hour' begins with a silent 'h', so the vowel sound needs 'an'.

chapter10.word: Find the error: "The teacher gave an advice to the students."
chapter10.explanation: 'Advice' is uncountable, so 'an' cannot be used → "gave advice".

chapter10.word: Find the error: "The higher you go, cooler it is."
chapter10.explanation: Parallel comparative structures need 'the' on both sides → "the cooler it is".

chapter10.word: Find the error: "He is the better than the two students."
options: the better than the two students
chapter10.explanation: When choosing between exactly two, use 'the + comparative + of', not 'than' → "the better of the two students".

chapter10.word: Find the error: "The treasurer and the secretary is present at the meeting."
options: The treasurer and the secretary is present
chapter10.explanation: Two articles ('the...the') indicate two different people, so a plural verb is needed → "are present".

chapter10.word: Find the error: "Death of his parents hurt him a lot."
chapter10.explanation: In a Noun + of + Noun structure, the first noun takes 'The' → "The death of his parents".

chapter10.word: Find the error: "He goes to the school regularly to study."
chapter10.explanation: Going for the primary purpose (studying) takes no article → "goes to school".

chapter10.word: Find the error: "a Mercedes, an Jaguar and an Fiat were parked outside."
chapter10.explanation: 'Jaguar' and 'Fiat' start with consonant sounds → "a Jaguar and a Fiat".

chapter10.word: Find the error: "The rich should help poor in every possible way."
chapter10.explanation: 'The + adjective' forms a class and needs 'the' throughout → "help the poor".

chapter11.word: Find the error: "I told Rahul on wait for two hours at the bus stop."
options: told Rahul on wait for two hours
chapter11.explanation: Imperatives in reported speech use 'to + V1' → "told Rahul to wait for two hours".

chapter11.word: Find the error: "Had I known, I should have done things differently."
options: I should have done things differently
chapter11.explanation: Inverted Type 3 follows the same 'would have' pattern → "I would have done things differently".

chapter11.word: Fill in the blank: Had he informed me earlier, I ______ arranged everything.
chapter11.explanation: Inverted Type 3 needs 'would have + V3'.

chapter11.word: Find the error: "I will help you provided you will tell the truth."
options: provided you will tell the truth
chapter11.explanation: The clause after 'provided' behaves like Type 1's if-clause — no 'will' → "provided you tell the truth".

chapter11.word: Find the error: "Had you been working, you had completed the task."
chapter11.explanation: Type 3 main clause needs 'would have + V3' → "you would have completed the task".

chapter11.word: Find the error: "I wish I studied harder for my exams."
chapter11.explanation: 'I wish' for past regret takes 'had + V3' → "I wish I had studied harder".

chapter11.word: Find the error: "Monika said to her mother that, 'I have passed.'"
chapter11.explanation: Direct speech after a reporting verb takes a comma, not 'that' → "said to her mother, 'I have passed.'"

chapter11.word: Find the error: "But for his help, the patient would die."
chapter11.explanation: 'But for' (unreal past condition) needs 'would have + V3' → "the patient would have died".

chapter11.word: Find the error: "Every Saturday, your mother prepares a pudding, isn't she?"
options: Every Saturday, your mother prepares a pudding
chapter11.explanation: Simple present, third person needs 'doesn't' → "doesn't she?"

chapter11.word: Find the error: "The child cried as if he was in pain."
options: as if he was in pain
chapter11.explanation: 'As if' for an imaginary/unreal state takes 'were' → "as if he were in pain".

chapter11.word: Find the error: "If you freeze water, it will become solid."
chapter11.explanation: For a universal scientific fact, both clauses use simple present → "it becomes solid".

chapter11.word: Fill in the blank: If it rains tomorrow, we ______ the picnic.
chapter11.explanation: Type 1 real future condition: if + simple present, main clause + will.

chapter11.word: Find the error: "I imagine you have learnt a lot, didn't you?"
options: I imagine you have learnt a lot
chapter11.explanation: The tag must match the auxiliary in the sentence (has/have) → "haven't you?"

chapter11.word: Fill in the blank: She wishes she ______ a better memory.
chapter11.explanation: 'Wish' for present regret takes simple past.

chapter11.word: Find the error: "If I was a clown, I would have made everyone smile."
options: I would have made everyone smile
chapter11.explanation: Type 2 always uses 'were', regardless of subject → "If I were a clown".

chapter11.word: Find the error: "He behaves if he were a king."
options: behaves if he were a king
chapter11.explanation: The correct phrase for pretence is 'as if', not just 'if' → "behaves as if he were a king".

chapter11.word: Find the error: "If he worked hard, he will surely get the job."
options: he will surely get the job
chapter11.explanation: Type 2 main clause needs 'would', not 'will' → "he would surely get the job".

chapter11.word: Find the error: "If it had not rained, they would not postpone the match."
options: they would not postpone the match
chapter11.explanation: Type 3 main clause needs 'would have + V3' → "would not have postponed".

chapter11.word: Find the error: "If she will exercise daily, she would remain energetic."
chapter11.explanation: Type 1 conditional never has 'will' in the if-clause → "If she exercises daily".

chapter11.word: Find the error: "Rahul's sister says that my brother is the best dancer in the city."
options: that my brother is the best dancer
chapter11.explanation: Pronouns change according to the actual speaker → "that her brother is the best dancer".

chapter11.word: Find the error: "She asked me where my hometown is."
chapter11.explanation: Reported speech with past reporting verb needs tense backshift → "where my hometown was".

chapter11.word: Fill in the blank: If you had asked for directions, you would not ______ lost now.
chapter11.explanation: Mixed conditional: past condition (had asked) + present result (would + V1 = be).

chapter11.word: Find the error: "If he had paid attention, he had not missed the train."
options: he had not missed the train
chapter11.explanation: The main clause of Type 3 needs 'would not have' → "he would not have missed the train".

chapter11.word: Fill in the blank: Unless you ______ hard, you will fail.
chapter11.explanation: 'Unless' (=if not) never takes 'not' or 'will' in its clause.

chapter11.word: Find the error: "Rishi asked Karan will he get a new football."
options: will he get a new football
chapter11.explanation: Yes/No questions in reported speech use 'if/whether' + statement order → "if he would get a new football".

chapter11.word: Fill in the blank: If she ______ earlier, she wouldn't have missed the flight.
chapter11.explanation: Type 3 if-clause needs 'had + V3'.

chapter11.word: Find the error: "He said that I have finished my work."
options: he said that I have finished my work
chapter11.explanation: With a past reporting verb, present perfect shifts to past perfect and pronouns change → "He said that he had finished his work."

chapter11.word: Find the error: "I wish I am taller than my brother."
chapter11.explanation: 'I wish' for present regret takes simple past/'were' → "I wish I were taller".

chapter11.word: Find the error: "If you study hard, you surely got selected."
chapter11.explanation: The main clause of Type 1 needs 'will' → "you will surely get selected".

chapter11.word: Find the error: "Let us work out the details, shouldn't we?"
options: Let us work out the details
chapter11.explanation: 'Let us' proposals always take the tag 'shall we?' → "shall we?"

chapter11.word: Find the error: "You cannot lead a healthy life although you stop smoking."
options: You cannot lead a healthy life
chapter11.explanation: The intended meaning ('if not') requires 'unless' → "unless you stop smoking".

chapter11.word: Find the error: "Suppose if you win the lottery, what will you do?"
options: Suppose if you win the lottery
chapter11.explanation: 'Suppose' and 'if' together are redundant → "Suppose you win the lottery".

chapter11.word: Find the error: "Rashmi works hard, don't she?"
chapter11.explanation: Simple present with third-person singular needs 'doesn't' → "doesn't she?"

chapter11.word: Fill in the blank: He behaves as if he ______ everything about the topic.
chapter11.explanation: 'As if' for pretence takes past tense.

chapter11.word: Fill in the blank: If I ______ you, I would apologize immediately.
chapter11.explanation: Type 2 conditional always uses 'were' for all subjects.

chapter12.word: Find the error: "The letter will be being written by her tomorrow."
chapter12.explanation: Future continuous has no valid passive form → "She will be writing a letter tomorrow" (active only).

chapter12.word: Convert to passive: "The government implemented the new policy."
options: The new policy was implemented by the government.
The new policy is implemented by the government.
The new policy implemented by the government.
The new policy has implemented by the government.
chapter12.explanation: Simple past active → was/were + V3.

chapter12.word: Convert to passive: "People believe that the government is judicious."
options: It is believed that the government is judicious.
That government is judicious is believed.
The government believed judicious by people.
chapter12.explanation: 'People say/believe that...' → 'It is believed that...'

chapter12.word: Convert to passive: "Please give me some money."
options: You are requested to give me some money.
chapter12.explanation: 'Please/Kindly' requests → 'You are requested to + V1'.

chapter12.word: Convert to passive: "He wrote the letter and posted it."
options: The letter was written and posted by him.
The letter was written by him and it was posted by him.
The letter written and posted by him.
The letter was written by him and posted.
chapter12.explanation: Compound sentences joined by 'and' need both clauses converted separately.

chapter12.word: Convert to passive: "The teacher made the students rewrite the assignment."
options: The students were made rewrite the assignment.
The students were made to rewrite the entire assignment.
The assignment made the students rewrite.
chapter12.explanation: Bare infinitive after 'make/see/hear' in active becomes 'to + V1' in passive.

chapter12.word: Convert to passive: "Did the organizers postpone the match?"
options: Was the match postponed by the organizers?
chapter12.explanation: 'Did' → 'was/were'; using 'did' in passive is incorrect.

chapter12.word: Convert to passive: "Scientists might have continuously analyzed the data."
options: The data might have been analyzed continuously by scientists.
The data might be analyzed by scientists.
The data might have analyzed by scientists.
chapter12.explanation: Perfect modal (might have + V3) → might + have + been + V3.

chapter12.word: Convert to passive: "He killed himself."
chapter12.explanation: Reflexive pronouns cannot become the subject; 'himself' stays as the agent.

chapter12.word: Convert to passive: "My father took me to the zoo, and I remember it."
options: I remember taken to the zoo by my father.
I remember being taken to the zoo by my father.
I remember to be taken to the zoo.
I remember took to the zoo.
chapter12.explanation: A gerund object becomes 'being + V3' in passive.

chapter12.word: Convert to passive: "Have the archivists digitized the medieval manuscripts?"
options: Have the medieval manuscripts been digitized by the archivists?
Had the medieval manuscripts been digitized?
chapter12.explanation: Has/have questions → Has/have + object + been + V3.

chapter12.word: Fill in the blank: She was satisfied ______ the result of the test. (VOICE Fixed Prep Table)
chapter12.explanation: 'Satisfied with' is the fixed passive preposition.

chapter12.word: Convert to passive: "The police are to catch the thieves."
options: The thieves are to be caught by the police.
The thieves are to be caught.
chapter12.explanation: When the doer is too obvious (police), 'by + object' can be dropped.

chapter12.word: Convert to passive: "The dogs fell upon me."
options: I was fallen upon by the dogs.
I was fallen by the dogs.
Upon me the dogs fell was.
chapter12.explanation: The verb-preposition combination ('fell upon') stays together right after V3, before 'by'.

chapter12.word: Convert to passive: "You must tell the truth."
options: The truth must be told by you.
chapter12.explanation: Modal + V1 → modal + be + V3.

chapter12.word: Convert to passive: "The teacher is checking the homework."
options: The homework is checked by the teacher.
The homework is being checked by the teacher.
The homework was being checked by the teacher.
The homework checks by the teacher.
chapter12.explanation: Present continuous active → is/am/are + being + V3.

chapter12.word: Convert to passive: "What had they done to the poor infrastructure?"
options: What had been done to the poor infrastructure by them?
What was done to the infrastructure?
What had they done by the infrastructure?
chapter12.explanation: 'What' stays first, followed by helping verb + been + V3.

chapter12.word: Convert to passive: "The audience had to listen to the presentation."
options: The presentation had to be listened to by the audience.
chapter12.explanation: 'Had to' + V1 → had to + be + V3, keeping the fixed preposition 'to'.

chapter12.word: Convert to passive: "Work hard."
options: You are advised to work hard.
chapter12.explanation: Imperative without an object → 'You are advised to + V1'.

chapter12.word: Convert to passive: "I had the mechanic wash the car."
options: The car was had washed by the mechanic.
The car had washed by the mechanic.
I was had the car washed.
chapter12.explanation: Causative 'have/get' constructions are already passive in sense; no double passive is formed.

chapter12.word: Find the error: "The proposal must have been reject by the board."
chapter12.explanation: After 'been', the verb must be in V3 form → "must have been rejected".

chapter12.word: Convert to passive: "The committee had rejected the proposal."
options: The proposal had been rejected by the committee.
The proposal has been rejected by the committee.
chapter12.explanation: Past perfect active → had + been + V3.

chapter12.word: Convert to passive: "Submit the documents to the head."
options: Let the documents be submitted to the head.
The documents submit to the head.
chapter12.explanation: Imperative (order) → Let + object + be + V3.

chapter12.word: Convert to passive: "Who painted the Mona Lisa?"
options: Who was the Mona Lisa painted?
By whom was the Mona Lisa painted?
The Mona Lisa was painted who?
chapter12.explanation: 'Who' (subject) → 'By whom' in passive.

chapter12.word: Convert to passive: "The new CEO has promised all employees a substantial bonus."
options: A substantial bonus has been promised by the new CEO.
All employees have been promised a substantial bonus by the new CEO.
All employees has promised a bonus.
A bonus has promised all employees.
chapter12.explanation: With a human and a non-human object, the human object becomes the subject in passive.

chapter12.word: Convert to passive: "Let her cook the meal."
options: Let the meal be cooked by her.
The meal is cooked by her.
Let her be cooked the meal.
chapter12.explanation: Active starting with 'Let' → Let + new object + be + V3 + by + old object.

chapter12.word: Convert to passive: "It is time to learn the guitar."
options: It is time the guitar is learned.
It is time for the guitar to be learned.
It is time to be learned the guitar.
It is time the guitar learns.
chapter12.explanation: 'It is time to' → 'It is time for + object + to be + V3'.

chapter12.word: Convert to passive: "We tasted the mango and found it sweet."
options: The mango is sweet when it is tasted.
The mango found sweet by us.
chapter12.explanation: Sensation verbs (taste, smell, feel) use the pattern 'Subject + is + Adjective + when + V3'.

chapter12.word: Convert to passive: "He is to write a book."
options: A book is written by him.
A book is to be written by him.
A book was to be written.
A book to write by him.
chapter12.explanation: 'To + V1' (infinitive) → 'to be + V3'.

chapter12.word: Fill in the blank: He is known ______ me for a long time. (VOICE Fixed Prep Table)
chapter12.explanation: 'Known to' (not 'by') is the fixed passive preposition.

chapter12.word: Fill in the blank: I was surprised ______ his sudden behaviour. (VOICE Fixed Prep Table)
chapter12.explanation: 'Surprised at' is the fixed passive preposition, not 'by'.

chapter12.word: Convert to passive: "Whom did she love?"
chapter12.explanation: 'Whom' (object) → 'Who' in passive.

chapter12.word: Fill in the blank: Gold is contained ______ this box. (VOICE Fixed Prep Table)
chapter12.explanation: 'Contained in' is the fixed passive preposition, not 'by'.

chapter12.word: Convert to passive: "They are going to start the project soon."
options: The project is going to be started soon.
The project is gone to start soon.
The project going to start soon.
The project was going to start.
chapter12.explanation: 'Going to' stays unchanged; add 'be + V3' after it.

chapter12.word: Convert to passive: "They elected him captain."
options: He was elected captain by them.
He was elected as captain by them.
chapter12.explanation: The person (him), not the title (captain), becomes the subject; and no 'as' is used with 'elect'.

chapter13.word: Convert to indirect: The child said to his mother, "Please help me."
options: The child requested his mother to please help him.
The child requested his mother to help him.
The child asked his mother please help him.
The child told his mother to help him please.
chapter13.explanation: 'Please/kindly' is dropped once 'requested' is used as the reporting verb.

chapter13.word: Convert to indirect: He said to me, "Where is the office?"
options: He asked me where was the office.
He asked me where the office was.
He asked me that where the office is.
He asked me where is the office.
chapter13.explanation: The wh-word itself connects the clauses; statement order follows.

chapter13.word: Convert to indirect: I said, "Let us start early."
