options: I suggested that we should start early.
I said let us start early.
I proposed us to start early.
chapter13.explanation: 'Let us' (proposal) becomes 'suggested/proposed that...should'.

chapter13.word: Convert to indirect: Karan said to me, "Good morning."
options: Karan said that good morning to me.
chapter13.explanation: Greetings use 'wished/bade', with no 'that'.

chapter13.word: Convert to indirect: He said, "The sun rises in the east."
options: He said that the sun rose in the east.
He said that the sun rises in the east.
He said that the sun had risen in the east.
He said that the sun will rise in the east.
chapter13.explanation: Universal truths never change tense, even after a past reporting verb.

chapter13.word: Convert to indirect: I said to him, "What are you doing there?"
options: I asked him what was he doing there.
I asked him what he was doing there.
I asked him that what he was doing there.
I asked him what is he doing there.
chapter13.explanation: Indirect questions use statement order (subject before verb), no inversion.

chapter13.word: Convert to indirect: Raghu said, "Meena, why have you been running?"
options: Raghu asked Meena why she had been running.
Raghu asked Meena why has she been running.
Raghu told Meena that why she had been running.
Raghu asked why Meena has been running.
chapter13.explanation: The vocative name becomes the object; tense shifts to past perfect continuous.

chapter13.word: Convert to indirect: She said, "I used to play the violin."
options: She said that she used to play the violin.
She said that she had used to play the violin.
She said that she would play the violin.
She said she uses to play the violin.
chapter13.explanation: 'Used to' never changes in reported speech.

chapter13.word: Convert to indirect: She said to me, "Will you take tea or coffee?"
options: She asked me if I would take tea or coffee.
She asked me whether I would take tea or coffee.
She asked that I would take tea or coffee.
She asked me if would I take tea or coffee.
chapter13.explanation: With an explicit choice ('or'), 'whether' is preferred over 'if'.

chapter13.word: Convert to indirect: He said to the manager, "Let me go."
options: He suggested the manager that he go.
He requested the manager to let him go.
He told the manager let him go.
He proposed the manager to let him go.
chapter13.explanation: 'Let me' (permission) becomes 'requested...to let him go'.

chapter13.word: Convert to indirect: The manager said, "Reporters report things accurately and readers trust them."
options: The manager said that reporters report things accurately and readers trust them.
The manager said that reporters reported things accurately and readers trusted them.
The manager said that reporters had reported things accurately.
The manager says that reporters reported things accurately.
chapter13.explanation: Past reporting verb shifts both clauses joined by 'and' to past tense.

chapter13.word: Find the error: "He asked me what was my name." (NARR — Redundancy/Misc R6)
chapter13.explanation: Indirect questions use statement word order → "what my name was".

chapter13.word: Convert to indirect: She said, "How wonderful the view is!"
options: She exclaimed how wonderful the view was.
She exclaimed that the view was very wonderful.
She said that how wonderful the view was.
She exclaimed that the view is wonderful.
chapter13.explanation: 'How/What a' exclamations become simple assertive sentences with 'very/great' added.

chapter13.word: Find the error: "He said to me, 'I have done my work.'" — convert to indirect and spot the error in this attempt: "He said me that he had done his work."
chapter13.explanation: 'Said' with a listener object must become 'told' → "He told me that".

chapter13.word: Convert to indirect: He said to me, "Are you fine?"
options: He asked me that I was fine.
He asked me if I was fine.
He asked me are you fine.
He asked if was I fine.
chapter13.explanation: Yes/No questions take 'if/whether' as the connector.

chapter13.word: Convert to indirect: He said to me, "You must work hard."
options: He said that I must work hard.
He told me that I had to work hard.
He told me that I must have worked hard.
He said I should work hard.
chapter13.explanation: 'Must' expressing obligation changes to 'had to' in reported speech.

chapter13.word: Convert to indirect: My grandmother said, "May you live long."
options: My grandmother wished that I live long.
My grandmother prayed that I might live long.
My grandmother said that I may live long.
My grandmother wished I lived long.
chapter13.explanation: Optative sentences (blessings) use 'prayed/wished that...might'.

chapter13.word: Convert to indirect: Mina said, "Do not touch the cable."
options: Mina forbade not to touch the cable.
Mina told not to touch the cable.
Mina ordered to not touch the cable.
chapter13.explanation: 'Forbade' already implies prohibition; adding 'not to' creates a double negative.

chapter13.word: Convert to indirect: Anurag said, "Alas! I have lost the match."
options: Anurag said sadly that he had lost the match.
Anurag exclaimed with sorrow that he had lost the match.
Anurag said alas he had lost the match.
Anurag exclaimed that alas he lost the match.
chapter13.explanation: The reporting verb changes to reflect emotion, and 'Alas' is dropped entirely.

chapter13.word: Convert to indirect: He said to me, "Where do you live?"
options: He asked me that where I lived.
He asked me where did I live.
He asked me where I lived.
He asked me where do I live.
chapter13.explanation: No 'that' with questions; question mark removed; statement word order used.

chapter13.word: Convert to indirect: Aman said to me, "Sir, please show me your ID card."
options: Aman said sir to show him the ID card.
Aman respectfully requested me to show him my ID card.
Aman requested me sir to show my ID card.
Aman asked me sir please to show ID.
chapter13.explanation: Terms of respect (Sir/Madam) are dropped, and 'respectfully' is added near the reporting verb.

chapter13.word: Convert to indirect: The man said to them, "Be quiet."
options: The man ordered them that they be quiet.
The man ordered them to be quiet.
The man said them to be quiet.
The man ordered them being quiet.
chapter13.explanation: Imperatives (positive) take 'to + V1' with no 'that'.

chapter13.word: Convert to indirect: He said to me, "Do you know the answer?"
options: He asked me if I know the answer.
He asked me if I knew the answer.
He asked me do I know the answer.
He asked me that I knew the answer.
chapter13.explanation: 'Do' is dropped and the main verb becomes past tense.

chapter13.word: Convert to indirect: He says, "I am building a model ship."
options: He says that he is building a model ship.
He said that he was building a model ship.
He says that he was building a model ship.
He says that he had built a model ship.
chapter13.explanation: Present-tense reporting verb ('says') means no tense backshift is needed.

chapter13.word: Find the error: "He said that that he was going."
chapter13.explanation: 'That' should be used only once → "He said that he was going."

chapter14.word: Find the error: "I love swimming, running, and to cycle."
chapter14.explanation: Parallel gerunds must match in form → "swimming, running, and cycling".

chapter14.word: Fill in the blank: A ______ of bees swarmed near the tree.
chapter14.explanation: Bees are collectively called a 'swarm'.

chapter14.word: Find the error: "Please revert back to me at your earliest."
chapter14.explanation: 'Revert' already means 'to go back'; 'back' is redundant → "revert to me".

chapter14.word: Find the error: "He shared his past history with the interviewer."
chapter14.explanation: 'History' is already about the past; 'past' is redundant → "his history".

chapter14.word: Find the error: "She has beautiful long hairs."
chapter14.explanation: 'Hair' (referring to a head of hair) is uncountable → "beautiful long hair".

chapter14.word: Find the error: "He let the students and I go home early."
chapter14.explanation: After 'let', use objective case → "let the students and me go".

chapter14.word: Find the error: "The bridge was completely destroyed in the flood."
chapter14.explanation: 'Destroyed' already means totally ruined; 'completely' is redundant → "was destroyed".

chapter14.word: Find the error: "He was accused of accepting bribes and lied about it."
options: accepting bribes and lied about it
chapter14.explanation: Parallel gerunds needed after 'accused of' → "accepting bribes and lying about it".

chapter14.word: Find the error: "Please describe about your experience."
chapter14.explanation: 'Describe' never takes 'about' → "describe your experience".

chapter14.word: Find the error: "The volcano arised suddenly last night."
chapter14.explanation: The correct past form of 'arise' is 'arose', not 'arised' → "arose suddenly".

chapter14.word: Fill in the blank: It violated the ______ (Principal/Principle) of natural justice.
chapter14.explanation: 'Principle' means a rule/doctrine; 'principal' means chief/main.

chapter14.word: Find the error: "By walk, it takes twenty minutes to reach the station."
options: it takes twenty minutes to reach the station
chapter14.explanation: The fixed phrase is 'on foot', not 'by walk' → "On foot, it takes twenty minutes".

chapter14.word: Find the error: "As soon as he arrived than the meeting started."
chapter14.explanation: 'As soon as' never pairs with 'than' → "the meeting started" (no 'than' needed).

chapter14.word: Find the error: "Female dog barked all night in the neighbourhood."
chapter14.explanation: A female dog is properly called a 'bitch' in formal grammar usage (fixed vocabulary point).

chapter14.word: Find the error: "All personnels must report to duty by 9 am."
chapter14.explanation: 'Personnel' is already plural; adding 's' is wrong → "All personnel must report".

chapter14.word: Find the error: "The Prime Minister Modi will address the nation today."
chapter14.explanation: When a name follows the title directly, no article is used → "Prime Minister Modi".

chapter14.word: Find the error: "She didn't eat none of the food I made."
chapter14.explanation: Double negatives are avoided; use 'any' → "didn't eat any of the food".

chapter14.word: Fill in the blank: A group of lions is called a ______.
chapter14.explanation: A group of lions is called a 'pride'.

chapter14.word: Fill in the blank: The ______ (Quiet/Quite) library was perfect for studying.
chapter14.explanation: 'Quiet' means silent; 'quite' means to a great extent.

chapter14.word: Find the error: "He wants to go to foreign for higher studies."
chapter14.explanation: The fixed phrase is 'go abroad', not 'go to foreign' → "go abroad".

chapter14.word: Fill in the blank: The city council decided to ______ (Raise/Rise) taxes next year.
chapter14.explanation: 'Raise' is transitive, needs an object (taxes).

chapter14.word: Find the error: "There is no boundation on how much you can earn here."
options: on how much you can earn here
chapter14.explanation: 'Boundation' is not a standard word; the correct word is 'compulsion' or 'restriction'.

chapter14.word: Fill in the blank: The reviewer had a great ______ (Affect/Effect) on my writing.
chapter14.explanation: 'Effect' is the noun (result); 'affect' is the verb.

chapter14.word: Find the error: "to kindly respond to this email at your convenience."
chapter14.explanation: Splitting the infinitive with an adverb is discouraged → "kindly to respond".

chapter14.word: Fill in the blank: Water levels ______ (Raise/Rise) rapidly during monsoon.
chapter14.explanation: 'Rise' is intransitive (subject moves up itself); 'raise' is transitive (requires an object).

chapter14.word: Fill in the blank: The judge gave his verdict ______ record time.
chapter14.explanation: The fixed idiom is 'in record time'.

chapter14.word: Find the error: "This happened the last before year."
chapter14.explanation: The correct phrase is 'the year before last' → "This happened the year before last."

chapter14.word: Fill in the blank: This laptop is, ______, the best in its price range.
chapter14.explanation: 'By far the best' is a fixed superlative-emphasis phrase.

chapter14.word: Find the error: "We saw many foots printed in the mud."
chapter14.explanation: The irregular plural of 'foot' is 'feet', not 'foots' → "many feet printed".

chapter14.word: Find the error: "The awkward tension between Sam and I made the room quiet."
chapter14.explanation: After the preposition 'between', use objective case → "between Sam and me".

chapter14.word: Fill in the blank: She managed to ______ (Adopt/Adapt) quickly to the new environment.
chapter14.explanation: 'Adapt' means to adjust; 'adopt' means to take on/accept formally.

chapter14.word: Find the error: "This is the final outcome of our research."
chapter14.explanation: 'Outcome' already means final result; 'final' is redundant → "the outcome of our research".

chapter14.word: Find the error: "Saroj is not only involved in organizing events but also in conducting them."
options: is not only involved in organizing events
chapter14.explanation: 'Not only...but also' should surround parallel prepositional phrases → "involved not only in organizing... but also in conducting".

chapter14.word: Find the error: "There was an unexpected surprise at the party."
chapter14.explanation: 'Surprise' already implies unexpectedness; redundant → "a surprise".

chapter14.word: Find the error: "Supposing if you fail, what will you do?"
chapter14.explanation: 'Supposing' and 'if' together are redundant → use only "Suppose you fail".

chapter15.word: Identify the phrase type: "HOLDING ONTO THE RIGGING FOR DEAR LIFE, I barely survived the storm."
chapter15.explanation: This phrase gives context to the whole sentence without being grammatically tied to it, so it is an absolute phrase.

chapter15.word: Identify the part of speech: "THIS is the unique problem."
chapter15.explanation: 'This' is the subject of the sentence with no noun following it, so it is a pronoun.

chapter15.word: Identify the clause type: "I cannot say WHEN HE COMES."
chapter15.explanation: The clause is the object of 'say', so it is a noun clause.

chapter15.word: Identify the Subject/Object role: "There was a lion roaring in the jungle."
options: 'A lion' is the real subject, 'There' is introductory
chapter15.explanation: 'There' is a dummy/introductory subject; the real subject is 'a lion'.

chapter15.word: Find the error: "I am having no house to live in."
chapter15.explanation: 'Have' meaning possession is stative → "I have no house to live in."

chapter15.word: Identify the Figure of Speech: "Parting is such sweet sorrow."
chapter15.explanation: 'Sweet' and 'sorrow' are contradictory terms combined together.

chapter15.word: Identify the clause type: "WHEN HE COMES, I will tell the truth."
chapter15.explanation: The clause tells 'when' the main action happens, functioning as an adverb clause of time.

chapter15.word: Identify the phrase type: "My father does not like MY GOING OUTSIDE."
chapter15.explanation: 'Going outside' acts as a noun (object of 'like'), so it is a gerund phrase.

chapter15.word: Identify the clause type: "I know the worker WHO IS DILIGENT."
chapter15.explanation: The clause describes 'worker', functioning as an adjective clause.

chapter15.word: Identify the Linking Verb usage: "He became an officer."
chapter15.explanation: 'Became' can be replaced by 'was' without changing the core meaning, so it's a linking verb.

chapter15.word: Identify the part of speech: "The meeting is OVER."
chapter15.explanation: 'Over' describes the state of the subject 'meeting' (finished), functioning as an adjective.

chapter15.word: Identify the part of speech: "I must EITHER work OR starve."
chapter15.explanation: 'Either' joins two choices (work/starve) with 'or', functioning as a conjunction.

chapter15.word: Identify the Verb type: "She got the first prize."
chapter15.explanation: 'Got' here shows the action of winning/receiving, so it functions as an action verb, not linking.

chapter15.word: Identify the phrase type: "Rohan, MY FRIEND, works hard."
chapter15.explanation: 'My friend' renames 'Rohan', so it is an appositive phrase.

chapter15.word: Identify the clause type: "I know WHAT YOU ARE SAYING."
chapter15.explanation: The clause acts as the object of 'know', so it is a noun clause.

chapter15.word: Identify the Word Formation: What is the noun form of "Receive"?
chapter15.explanation: 'Receipt' is the standard noun form; 'receptive' is an adjective.

chapter15.word: Identify the Word Formation: What is the noun form of "Evade"?
chapter15.explanation: 'Evasion' is the noun; 'evasive' is the adjective form.

chapter15.word: Identify the part of speech: "SOME girlfriends are very toxic."
chapter15.explanation: 'Some' quantifies the noun 'girlfriends', so it is an adjective here.

chapter15.word: Identify the Figure of Speech: "The wind whispered through the trees."
chapter15.explanation: The wind (non-living) is given the human quality of whispering.

chapter15.word: Find the error: "He is owning a car."
chapter15.explanation: 'Own' is a stative verb (possession) and cannot take continuous form → "He owns a car."

chapter15.word: Identify the part of speech: "My beloved is PRETTY good in dancing."
chapter15.explanation: 'Pretty' modifies the adjective 'good' (meaning 'quite'), so it functions as an adverb.

chapter15.word: Find the error: "The sweet tasted deliciously."
chapter15.explanation: 'Taste' as a linking verb takes an adjective, not an adverb → "tasted delicious."

chapter15.word: Identify the part of speech: "None BUT the brave deserves the fair."
chapter15.explanation: 'But' here means 'except', functioning as a preposition.

chapter15.word: Identify the part of speech: "THIS house belongs to her."
chapter15.explanation: 'This' precedes the noun 'house' and modifies it, so it is an adjective.

chapter15.word: Identify the part of speech: "He fell OVER."
chapter15.explanation: 'Over' modifies the verb 'fell' with no object, functioning as an adverb.

chapter15.word: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: "Please come IN."
chapter15.explanation: 'In' modifies the verb 'come' with no object following, so it functions as an adverb.

chapter15.word: Identify the Word Formation: What is the adjective form of "Voice"?
chapter15.explanation: 'Vocal' is the correct adjective form of 'Voice'.

chapter15.word: Identify the Complement type: "We made him monitor."
chapter15.explanation: 'Monitor' completes information about the object 'him', so it is an object complement.

chapter15.word: Identify the clause type: "This is the time WHEN HE COMES."
chapter15.explanation: The clause modifies the noun 'time', so it is an adjective clause.

chapter15.word: Identify the phrase type: "A BURNING TRAIN was seen from a distance."
chapter15.explanation: 'Burning' modifies the noun 'train' as an adjective, so it is a present participle phrase.

chapter15.word: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: "He runs FAST."
chapter15.explanation: 'Fast' modifies the verb 'runs', telling how he runs — Adverb.

chapter15.word: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: "She has a KIND heart."
chapter15.explanation: 'Kind' describes the noun 'heart' — Adjective.

chapter15.word: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: "WOW, what a goal!"
chapter15.explanation: 'Wow' expresses sudden emotion, standing independently — Interjection.

chapter15.word: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: "He walked ACROSS the bridge."
chapter15.explanation: 'Across' relates 'bridge' to the rest of the sentence, showing position — Preposition.

chapter15.word: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: "EITHER you OR I am wrong."
chapter15.explanation: 'Either...or' joins two alternatives — a correlative Conjunction.

chapter15.word: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: "The FAST train left early."
chapter15.explanation: Here 'fast' qualifies the noun 'train' — Adjective (same word, different POS by context).

chapter15.word: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: "HONESTY is the best policy."
chapter15.explanation: 'Honesty' names a quality, not a tangible thing — Abstract Noun.

chapter15.word: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: "I bought a HERD of cattle."
chapter15.explanation: 'Herd' names a group/collection of cattle — Collective Noun.

chapter15.word: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: "This book is MINE."
chapter15.explanation: 'Mine' stands alone in place of 'my book' — Possessive Pronoun (not followed by a noun).

chapter15.word: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: "This is MY book."
chapter15.explanation: 'My' directly qualifies the noun 'book' — Possessive Adjective (determiner).

chapter15.word: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: "He hurt HIMSELF while playing."
chapter15.explanation: 'Himself' refers back to the subject and is essential to the meaning — Reflexive Pronoun.

chapter15.word: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: "I MYSELF saw the accident."
chapter15.explanation: 'Myself' here only adds emphasis and can be removed without changing meaning — Emphatic Pronoun.

chapter15.word: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: "SOMEBODY left the door open."
chapter15.explanation: 'Somebody' does not refer to any specific person — Indefinite Pronoun.

chapter15.word: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: "The book, WHICH I bought yesterday, is interesting."
chapter15.explanation: 'Which' relates back to 'book' and introduces a clause about it — Relative Pronoun.

chapter15.word: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: "He works HARD to earn a living."
chapter15.explanation: 'Hard' modifies the verb 'works', showing manner — Adverb.

chapter15.word: Identify the phrase type: "READING BOOKS is his favourite hobby."
chapter15.explanation: 'Reading books' acts as the subject and is built on a gerund (V-ing used as a noun) — Gerund Phrase.

chapter15.word: Identify the phrase type: "He wants TO WIN THE MATCH."
chapter15.explanation: 'To win the match' begins with 'to + verb' functioning as the object — Infinitive Phrase.

chapter15.word: Identify the phrase type: "THE BOY IN THE BLUE SHIRT is my brother."
chapter15.explanation: 'In the blue shirt' describes 'the boy' like an adjective — Adjective Phrase.

chapter15.word: Identify the phrase type: "SITTING BY THE WINDOW, she watched the rain."
chapter15.explanation: 'Sitting by the window' modifies the subject 'she' as an adjective would — Participle Phrase.

chapter15.word: Identify the phrase type: "THE WEATHER BEING PLEASANT, we went for a walk."
chapter15.explanation: This phrase has its own subject ('weather') and participle, independent of the main clause — Absolute Phrase.

chapter15.word: Identify the phrase type: "He lives IN A SMALL VILLAGE."
chapter15.explanation: 'In a small village' begins with a preposition and shows place — Prepositional Phrase.

chapter15.word: Identify the phrase type: "He behaved IN A VERY RUDE MANNER."
chapter15.explanation: 'In a very rude manner' modifies the verb 'behaved', telling how — Adverb Phrase (functioning as adverb).

chapter15.word: Identify the phrase type: "THE OLD WOODEN HOUSE stood on the hill."
chapter15.explanation: 'The old wooden house' is a group of words centred on the noun 'house', acting as subject — Noun Phrase.

chapter15.word: Identify the phrase type: "She HAS BEEN WORKING here since 2015."
chapter15.explanation: 'Has been working' is a group of auxiliary + main verbs forming the predicate — Verb Phrase.

chapter15.word: Identify the phrase type: "EXHAUSTED FROM THE JOURNEY, he fell asleep instantly."
chapter15.explanation: 'Exhausted from the journey' modifies 'he' and is built on a past participle — Participle Phrase.

chapter15.word: Identify the phrase type: "TO ERR is human, TO FORGIVE divine."
chapter15.explanation: 'To err' and 'to forgive' function as subjects and begin with 'to + verb' — Infinitive Phrase.

chapter15.word: Identify the phrase type: "His main hobby is COLLECTING OLD COINS."
chapter15.explanation: 'Collecting old coins' completes the subject complement using -ing as a noun — Gerund Phrase.

chapter15.word: Identify the phrase type: "The man STANDING AT THE GATE is a stranger."
chapter15.explanation: 'Standing at the gate' describes 'the man' like an adjective — Participle Phrase.

chapter15.word: Identify the phrase type: "AFTER THE HEAVY RAIN, the roads were flooded."
chapter15.explanation: 'After the heavy rain' tells when the roads were flooded, modifying the verb — Adverb Phrase.

chapter15.word: Identify the phrase type: "I saw A TALL DARK STRANGER at the door."
chapter15.explanation: 'A tall dark stranger' is a group of words built around the noun 'stranger', used as the object — Noun Phrase.

chapter15.word: Identify the phrase type: "This is a matter OF GREAT IMPORTANCE."
chapter15.explanation: 'Of great importance' begins with a preposition and describes 'matter' — Prepositional Phrase.

chapter15.word: Identify the phrase type: "He is EASY TO PLEASE."
chapter15.explanation: 'To please' begins with 'to + verb', completing the adjective 'easy' — Infinitive Phrase.

chapter15.word: Identify the phrase type: "TIRED AND HUNGRY, the travellers stopped at an inn."
chapter15.explanation: 'Tired and hungry' is a group of adjectives describing 'the travellers' — Adjective Phrase.

chapter15.word: Identify the clause type: "I know THAT HE IS HONEST."
chapter15.explanation: 'That he is honest' is the object of 'know' — Noun Clause.

chapter15.word: Identify the clause type: "This is the house WHERE I WAS BORN."
chapter15.explanation: 'Where I was born' describes the noun 'house' — Adjective (Relative) Clause.

chapter15.word: Identify the clause type: "WHEN THE BELL RANG, the students left."
chapter15.explanation: 'When the bell rang' tells the time of the main action — Adverb Clause of Time.

chapter15.word: Identify the clause type: "The boy WHO WON THE RACE is my friend."
chapter15.explanation: 'Who won the race' describes 'the boy' — Adjective (Relative) Clause.

chapter15.word: Identify the clause type: "WHAT HE SAID surprised everyone."
chapter15.explanation: 'What he said' is the subject of the sentence — Noun Clause.

chapter15.word: Identify the clause type: "She sang so well THAT EVERYONE APPLAUDED."
chapter15.explanation: 'That everyone applauded' shows the result of 'so well' — Adverb Clause of Result.

chapter15.word: Identify the clause type: "IF IT RAINS, we will stay indoors."
chapter15.explanation: 'If it rains' states a condition for the main clause — Adverb Clause of Condition.

chapter15.word: Identify the clause type: "AS HE WAS TIRED, he went to bed early."
chapter15.explanation: 'As he was tired' gives the reason for going to bed early — Adverb Clause of Reason.

chapter15.word: Identify the clause type: "He behaved AS IF HE WERE THE BOSS."
chapter15.explanation: 'As if he were the boss' describes how he behaved — Adverb Clause of Manner.

chapter15.word: Identify the clause type: "He is taller THAN HIS BROTHER IS."
chapter15.explanation: 'Than his brother is' compares the degree of tallness — Adverb Clause of Comparison.

chapter15.word: Identify the clause type: "I do not know WHY HE LEFT SO SOON."
chapter15.explanation: 'Why he left so soon' is the object of 'know' — Noun Clause.

chapter15.word: Identify the clause type: "Sit WHEREVER YOU LIKE."
chapter15.explanation: 'Wherever you like' tells the place of sitting — Adverb Clause of Place.

chapter15.word: Identify the clause type: "THOUGH HE IS RICH, he is not happy."
chapter15.explanation: 'Though he is rich' shows a contrast/concession to the main clause — Adverb Clause of Concession.

chapter15.word: Identify the clause type: "This is the reason WHY HE FAILED."
chapter15.explanation: 'Why he failed' describes the noun 'reason' — Adjective Clause.

chapter15.word: Identify the clause type: "He ran so fast THAT HE COULD NOT BE CAUGHT."
chapter15.explanation: 'That he could not be caught' expresses the result of running fast — Adverb Clause of Result.

chapter15.word: Identify the clause type in the sentence: "He said THAT HE WOULD COME."
chapter15.explanation: 'That he would come' is the object of 'said' — Noun Clause.

chapter15.word: Identify the underlined clause: "HE WON THE MATCH" in "He won the match, and the crowd cheered."
chapter15.explanation: This clause can stand alone as a complete sentence — Independent (Main) Clause.

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "Is life worth living? It depends on the liver."
chapter16.explanation: 'Liver' has a double meaning (organ / one who lives) — a Pun.

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "We shall fight on the beaches, we shall fight on the hills."
chapter16.explanation: Repeating "we shall fight" at the start of successive clauses is Anaphora.

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "I have told you a million times not to lie."
chapter16.explanation: An extreme exaggeration ('a million times') is Hyperbole.

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "Pitter-patter of little feet."
chapter16.explanation: Repetition of consonant sounds within and at the end of words (not just the start) is Consonance.

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "She sells seashells on the seashore."
chapter16.explanation: Repetition of the initial 's' sound across nearby words is Alliteration.

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "The child is the father of the man."
chapter16.explanation: A self-contradictory statement that reveals a deeper truth is a Paradox.

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "Speech is silver, silence is golden."
chapter16.explanation: Two contrasting ideas placed side by side form an Antithesis.

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "Cowards die many times before their death."
chapter16.explanation: The statement seems impossible literally but conveys a truth about fear — Paradox.

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "Government of the people, by the people, for the people."
chapter16.explanation: Repeating "the people" at the end of successive phrases is Epiphora (Epistrophe).

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "Illiterate him from memory." (should be 'obliterate')
chapter16.explanation: The mistaken use of a similar-sounding word for comic/erroneous effect is Malapropism.

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "O wild west wind, thou breath of Autumn's being!"
chapter16.explanation: Directly addressing an inanimate/abstract thing (wind) as if alive is Apostrophe.

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "He stole my heart and my wallet."
chapter16.explanation: One verb ('stole') used with two different senses/objects at once is Zeugma.

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "The golden yellow sunlight filtered through the trees."
chapter16.explanation: Vivid sensory description that creates a mental picture is Imagery.

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "For Brutus is an honourable man." (said sarcastically)
chapter16.explanation: The intended meaning is the opposite of the literal words — Verbal Irony.

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "My friends were poor but honest."
chapter16.explanation: This subtly suggests rich people are usually dishonest — an indirect implication, Innuendo.

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "Animal Farm represents the Russian Revolution."
chapter16.explanation: A whole narrative symbolizing a deeper political/moral meaning is an Allegory.

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "He had a lazy chair."
chapter16.explanation: The adjective 'lazy' actually describes the person, not the chair — Transferred Epithet.

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "He cried a river of tears."
chapter16.explanation: A deliberate exaggeration for emotional effect is Hyperbole.

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "He is a lion in the battlefield."
chapter16.explanation: A direct comparison without 'like/as' is a Metaphor.

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "I feel the need for speed."
chapter16.explanation: Repetition of the vowel sound "ee" within nearby words is Assonance.

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "All hands on deck!"
chapter16.explanation: 'Hands' (a part of the body) represents the whole sailors — Synecdoche.

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "Passed away" (instead of 'died').
chapter16.explanation: A milder expression replacing a harsh term is a Euphemism.

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "Burning fire"
chapter16.explanation: 'Fire' already implies burning; adding a redundant descriptive word is Pleonasm.

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "Who doesn't want success?"
chapter16.explanation: A question asked for effect, with an obvious answer, is a Rhetorical Question.

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "Free gift"
chapter16.explanation: 'Gift' already implies 'free'; repeating the same idea in different words is Tautology.

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "Boom, crash, bang!"
chapter16.explanation: Words that imitate natural sounds are Onomatopoeia.

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "Open secret."
chapter16.explanation: A short two-word combination of contradictory terms is Oxymoron.

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "He was a Romeo to the girls in college."
chapter16.explanation: A reference to a famous literary character (Romeo) is an Allusion.

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "Just as a sword is the weapon of a warrior, a pen is the weapon of a writer."
chapter16.explanation: Comparing an unfamiliar idea to a familiar one to explain it is an Analogy.

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "The pen is mightier than the sword."
chapter16.explanation: 'Pen' and 'sword' stand for related concepts (writing and violence) — Metonymy.

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "Never let a fool kiss you, or a kiss fool you."
chapter16.explanation: The reversed word order pattern (AB-BA) is Chiasmus.

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "War is peace; freedom is slavery; ignorance is strength."
chapter16.explanation: These statements seem self-contradictory but suggest a deeper political truth — Paradox.

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "It was the best of times, it was the worst of times."
chapter16.explanation: Two sharply contrasting ideas placed together form an Antithesis.

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "Not bad at all!" (meaning very good)
chapter16.explanation: Using a negative to express a positive meaning is Litotes (understatement).

chapter16.word: Identify the figure of speech: "The king of the jungle" (referring to a lion)
chapter16.explanation: Using a roundabout phrase instead of the direct word ('lion') is Periphrasis (Circumlocution).

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "He is poor, yet he is honest."
chapter17.explanation: Two independent clauses joined by 'yet' — Compound.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "Although he was ill, he went to school."
chapter17.explanation: A dependent clause ('Although he was ill') + an independent clause — Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "He went to the shop and bought some fruits."
chapter17.explanation: One subject with a compound predicate — Simple.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "He confessed that he had stolen the money."
chapter17.explanation: 'That he had stolen the money' is a dependent noun clause — Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "He ran fast, but he missed the train."
chapter17.explanation: Two independent clauses joined by the coordinating conjunction 'but' — Compound.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "She opened the door and found a puppy."
chapter17.explanation: One subject with a compound predicate (two verbs, same subject) is still Simple.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "He cleaned the house, cooked food, and then went out for a walk."
chapter17.explanation: One subject, three verbs in a compound predicate — Simple.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "Having finished his dinner, he went to bed and dreamed about his childhood."

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "Unless you work hard, you will not succeed."
chapter17.explanation: 'Unless you work hard' is a dependent (subordinate) clause — Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "I wanted to help him, but he refused my offer because he was angry."
chapter17.explanation: Two independent clauses ('I wanted...', 'he refused...') + one dependent clause ('because he was angry') — Compound-Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "While he was preparing for exams, his friends went to the park, and he stayed home to study."
chapter17.explanation: One dependent clause + two independent clauses joined by 'and' — Compound-Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "I don't know why he left early."
chapter17.explanation: 'Why he left early' is a dependent noun clause — Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "Ravi is a kind man who helps the poor."
chapter17.explanation: 'Who helps the poor' is a dependent relative clause — Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "He speaks English fluently and writes French with ease."
chapter17.explanation: Same subject with a compound predicate — Simple.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "Though he is rich, he lives a simple life, and people respect him."
chapter17.explanation: One dependent clause ('Though he is rich') + two independent clauses joined by 'and' — Compound-Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "I will call you when I reach home."
chapter17.explanation: One independent clause + one dependent clause ('when I reach home') — Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the Clause structure: "IF YOU HELP ME, I will help you."
chapter17.explanation: 'If' is a subordinating conjunction introducing a dependent clause — Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "She said that she had finished her work but that she was still tired."
chapter17.explanation: One independent clause + two dependent noun clauses — Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "She was late because the bus broke down, and she missed the meeting."
chapter17.explanation: Two independent clauses joined by 'and' + one dependent clause ('because the bus broke down') — Compound-Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "The train was late, so we waited at the station until it arrived."
chapter17.explanation: Two independent clauses joined by 'so' + one dependent clause ('until it arrived') — Compound-Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "Working hard, he passed the exam."
chapter17.explanation: A single subject with a participle phrase and one finite verb — Simple.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "Despite the heavy rain, the match continued."
chapter17.explanation: One independent clause with a prepositional phrase — Simple.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "She sings and dances beautifully."
chapter17.explanation: One subject with a compound verb (sings, dances) — Simple.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "On seeing the police, the thief ran away."
chapter17.explanation: One subject, one finite verb, with a participial phrase — Simple.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "He is too weak to walk."
chapter17.explanation: One clause with an infinitive phrase, no subordinate clause — Simple.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "The rising sun looked beautiful."
chapter17.explanation: One subject 'sun' with a participle adjective 'rising' — Simple.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "He must have missed the train."
chapter17.explanation: One subject and one finite verb phrase — Simple.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "To err is human."
chapter17.explanation: A single clause with an infinitive phrase as subject — Simple.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "Being ill, he stayed at home."
chapter17.explanation: One independent clause preceded by a participle phrase — Simple.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "She left the room without saying a word."
chapter17.explanation: One subject and verb, with a gerund phrase — Simple.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "In spite of his poverty, he is happy."
chapter17.explanation: A single independent clause with a prepositional phrase — Simple.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "The teacher entered the class and greeted the students."
chapter17.explanation: One subject with a compound predicate joined by 'and' — Simple.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "He decided to leave the job."
chapter17.explanation: One clause with an infinitive as object, no separate clause — Simple.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "Owing to the storm, the flight was delayed."
chapter17.explanation: One independent clause with a prepositional phrase of reason — Simple.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "I saw him crossing the road."
chapter17.explanation: One clause with a participle phrase as object complement — Simple.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "He was tired, but he kept working."
chapter17.explanation: Two independent clauses joined by 'but' — Compound.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "Either you apologise, or you leave this house."
chapter17.explanation: Two independent clauses joined by 'or' — Compound.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "It was raining, so we cancelled the picnic."
chapter17.explanation: Two independent clauses joined by 'so' — Compound.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "Not only did he apologise, but he also paid the fine."
chapter17.explanation: Two independent clauses joined by 'not only...but also' — Compound.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "He is poor; he is honest, however."
chapter17.explanation: Two independent clauses joined with a semicolon and connector — Compound.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "She was late, yet she completed the task."
chapter17.explanation: Two independent clauses joined by 'yet' — Compound.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "He neither called nor wrote to me."
chapter17.explanation: Two independent ideas linked by the correlative 'neither...nor' with a shared subject — Compound.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "Study hard, and you will succeed."
chapter17.explanation: Two independent clauses joined by 'and' (imperative + result) — Compound.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "He wanted to go, but his mother stopped him."
chapter17.explanation: Two independent clauses joined by 'but' — Compound.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "The sun set, and darkness fell."
chapter17.explanation: Two independent clauses joined by 'and' — Compound.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "I called him, but he did not answer."
chapter17.explanation: Two independent clauses joined by 'but' — Compound.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "He is rich, still he is unhappy."
chapter17.explanation: Two independent clauses joined by the conjunction 'still' — Compound.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "Run fast, or you will miss the bus."
chapter17.explanation: Two independent clauses (imperative + consequence) joined by 'or' — Compound.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "He apologised, and she forgave him."
chapter17.explanation: Two independent clauses joined by 'and' — Compound.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "She is intelligent; moreover, she is hardworking."
chapter17.explanation: Two independent clauses linked by 'moreover' — Compound.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "He said that he was innocent."
chapter17.explanation: A dependent noun clause ('that he was innocent') + main clause — Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "The man who helped me yesterday is my neighbour."
chapter17.explanation: A dependent adjective clause ('who helped me yesterday') + main clause — Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "When the teacher entered, the students stood up."
chapter17.explanation: A dependent adverb clause of time + main clause — Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "I do not know where he lives."
chapter17.explanation: A dependent noun clause ('where he lives') as object — Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "Because he was late, he missed the bus."
chapter17.explanation: A dependent adverb clause of reason + main clause — Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "This is the book that I bought yesterday."
chapter17.explanation: A dependent adjective clause ('that I bought yesterday') + main clause — Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "If you work hard, you will succeed."
chapter17.explanation: A dependent adverb clause of condition + main clause — Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "She asked me what I wanted."
chapter17.explanation: A dependent noun clause ('what I wanted') as object — Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "As soon as he arrived, the meeting began."
chapter17.explanation: A dependent adverb clause of time + main clause — Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "He is a man whom everybody trusts."
chapter17.explanation: A dependent adjective clause ('whom everybody trusts') + main clause — Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "Since he had no money, he could not buy the book."
chapter17.explanation: A dependent adverb clause of reason + main clause — Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "Whoever comes first will get the prize."
chapter17.explanation: A dependent noun clause ('whoever comes first') as subject — Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "Although he tried hard, he failed."
chapter17.explanation: A dependent adverb clause of concession + main clause — Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "I remember the day when we first met."
chapter17.explanation: A dependent adjective clause ('when we first met') + main clause — Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "He ran so fast that he won the race."
chapter17.explanation: A dependent adverb clause of result ('that he won the race') + main clause — Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "Tell me what happened."
chapter17.explanation: A dependent noun clause ('what happened') as object — Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "The place where I was born is beautiful."
chapter17.explanation: A dependent adjective clause ('where I was born') + main clause — Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "Unless you work hard, you will not pass."
chapter17.explanation: A dependent adverb clause of condition ('unless...') + main clause — Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "He behaved as if he knew everything."
chapter17.explanation: A dependent adverb clause of manner ('as if he knew everything') + main clause — Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "I believe that honesty is the best policy."
chapter17.explanation: A dependent noun clause ('that honesty is the best policy') as object — Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "He was tired, but he finished the work because he had promised to."
chapter17.explanation: Two independent clauses ('he was tired, but he finished the work') + a dependent clause ('because he had promised to') — Compound-Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "She went to the market, and she bought vegetables that were fresh."
chapter17.explanation: Two independent clauses joined by 'and' + a dependent adjective clause ('that were fresh') — Compound-Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "I called him, but he did not answer because he was sleeping."
chapter17.explanation: Two independent clauses + a dependent clause of reason — Compound-Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "He studied hard, and he passed the exam that he had feared."
chapter17.explanation: Two independent clauses + a dependent adjective clause — Compound-Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "Although it was raining, we went out, and we got soaked."
chapter17.explanation: A dependent clause + two independent clauses joined by 'and' — Compound-Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "He is poor, but he is happy because he is content with life."
chapter17.explanation: Two independent clauses + a dependent clause of reason — Compound-Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "When the bell rang, the students left, but the teacher stayed back."
chapter17.explanation: A dependent clause + two independent clauses joined by 'but' — Compound-Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "She wanted to travel, so she saved money that she earned every month."
chapter17.explanation: Two independent clauses + a dependent adjective clause — Compound-Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "He knew that he was wrong, but he did not apologise."
chapter17.explanation: A dependent noun clause + two independent clauses joined by 'but' — Compound-Complex.

chapter17.word: Identify the sentence type: "I finished my homework, and I watched a movie that I had wanted to see."
chapter17.explanation: Two independent clauses + a dependent adjective clause — Compound-Complex.

chapter18.word: Fill in the blank: You are coming to the party, ______?
chapter18.explanation: A positive statement takes a negative tag.

chapter18.word: Fill in the blank: Each of the students has submitted the assignment, ______?
chapter18.explanation: 'Each' takes a singular verb ('has'), so the tag matches singular → "hasn't he?"

chapter18.word: Fill in the blank: Let us finish this task first, ______?
chapter18.explanation: 'Let us' proposals always take 'shall we?'

chapter18.word: Find the error: "Rashmi works hard, don't she?"
chapter18.explanation: Third-person singular in simple present needs 'doesn't' → "doesn't she?"

chapter18.word: Fill in the blank: I am your friend, ______?
chapter18.explanation: 'Amn't' is not standard English; the correct tag for 'I am' is 'aren't I?'

chapter18.word: Find the error: "The trains in India never come on time, aren't they?"
options: The trains in India never come on time
chapter18.explanation: 'Never' already makes the statement negative, so the tag should be positive → "do they?"

chapter18.word: Fill in the blank: She can't swim, ______?
chapter18.explanation: A negative statement takes a positive tag.

chapter18.word: Find the error: "We have already met each other, didn't we?"
options: We have already met each other
chapter18.explanation: Present perfect statement needs 'haven't we?' as the tag.

chapter18.word: Find the error: "The new HR was late on his first day, weren't he?"
options: The new HR was late on his first day
chapter18.explanation: Singular subject 'he' with 'was' needs 'wasn't he?' as the tag.

chapter18.word: Find the error: "None of his colleagues came to the party, have they?"
options: None of his colleagues came to the party
chapter18.explanation: Simple past statement needs the tag 'did they?' not 'have they?'

chapter18.word: Fill in the blank: This is not the correct answer, ______?
chapter18.explanation: A negative statement takes a positive tag.

chapter18.word: Fill in the blank: He seldom visits us, ______?
chapter18.explanation: 'Seldom' is already negative, so the tag stays positive → "does he?"

chapter18.word: Find the error: "Let's go for a dinner, will we?"
chapter18.explanation: 'Let's' proposals always take the tag 'shall we?'

chapter18.word: Find the error: "I imagine you have learnt a lot, didn't you?"
options: I imagine you have learnt a lot
chapter18.explanation: Present perfect tag must match the auxiliary 'have' → "haven't you?"

chapter18.word: Fill in the blank: Nobody called me yesterday, ______?
chapter18.explanation: 'Nobody' is negative and takes the plural pronoun 'they' in the tag, kept positive.

chapter18.word: Fill in the blank: The team is divided in its opinion, ______?
chapter18.explanation: When the collective noun acts as a single unit, the tag is singular.

chapter18.word: Find the error: "You haven't seen the film I recommended, did you?"
options: You haven't seen the film I recommended
chapter18.explanation: The negative auxiliary 'haven't' in the statement must be echoed positively → "have you?"

chapter18.word: Find the error: "An Aspirant should be consistent in his studies, don't he?"
options: An Aspirant should be consistent in his studies
chapter18.explanation: The modal 'should' needs the tag 'shouldn't he?'

chapter18.word: Find the error: "All of you were present there, weren't they?"
options: All of you were present there
chapter18.explanation: The subject is 'you', so the tag must also be 'you' → "weren't you?"

chapter18.word: Find the error: "Everybody has come on time, hasn't he?"
chapter18.explanation: Indefinite pronouns like 'Everybody' always take the plural tag 'they' → "haven't they?"

chapter19.word: Find the error: "He is much taller than any boy in his class." (Mixed — Adjective R15)
chapter19.explanation: Since he is part of the group being compared, 'other' must be added → "any other boy in his class".

chapter19.word: Find the error: "She asked me that where I was going in such a hurry." (Mixed — Narration R10)
chapter19.explanation: 'That' is redundant before a wh-word question in indirect speech → "asked me where I was going".

chapter19.word: Find the error: "Neither the manager nor the employees has noticed the change." (Mixed — SVA R2)
options: Neither the manager nor the employees

chapter19.explanation: 'Both...and' always takes a plural verb → "are present today".
